translations.text: These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel on the other side of the Jordan, near the wilderness, in the western regions opposite the Red Sea, between Paran, Tophel, Laban, and Aulon.
It is eleven days from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea by the road through Mount Seir.
In the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Moses spoke before all the Israelites, telling them everything the Lord had commanded him to tell them.
This was after he had killed Sihon, king of the Amorites, and Og, king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
On the other side of the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain this law to them, saying:
The Lord our God spoke to us at Horeb, saying, “You have stayed long enough on this mountain.

Turn now, set out, and go into the hill country of the Amorites and to all those who live in the Arabah, the mountains, and the plain, and to the western region and the coast, the land of the Canaanites and the Anti-Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates.

Take notice: I have placed this land before you and given it into your hands so that you may enter and take possession of it. It is the land I swore to give to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and to their descendants after them.”
And at that time I told you, “I cannot bear the burden of you by myself.”
The Lord your God has increased your numbers, and look, today you are as numerous as the stars of heaven.
May the Lord, the God of your ancestors, increase you still further, making you thousands of times more numerous, and bless you as he promised you.
How can I bear your troubles, your conflicts, and your quarrels?
Choose from among yourselves wise, learned, and discerning men from your tribes, and appoint them as leaders over you.
You answered me, saying, “What you have proposed is good to do.”
I took wise, learned, and discerning men from among you and appointed them over you as leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, and as officials to lead you.
At that time I instructed your judges, saying, “Hear disputes between fellow Israelites, and judge fairly between a person and his fellow Israelite, and between a person and a foreign resident.

Do not show favoritism in judgment. Judge the small and the great alike, and do not defer to anyone, because judgment belongs to God. Bring any case that is too difficult for you to me, and I will hear it.”
At that time I commanded you concerning everything you were to do.

We set out from Horeb and traveled through that entire vast and terrifying wilderness that you saw, along the road to the hill country of the Amorites, because the Lord our God had commanded us. We came to Kadesh-barnea.
I said to you, “You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which the Lord our God will give you.

See how the Lord your God has placed the land before you so that you may go up and take possession of it, as the Lord, the God of your ancestors, told you. Do not be afraid or lose courage before them.”
All of you approached me and said to me, “Let us send men ahead of us to explore the land for us and report to us about the road we should travel and the cities we will enter.”
What you proposed pleased me, and I chose twelve men from among you, one man from each tribe.
They turned and went up into the hill country, came to the Valley of the Grape Cluster, and explored the land.
And they took some of the land’s fruit in their hands and brought it to us, saying to us, “The land that the Lord our God will give us is good.”
But you were unwilling to go up. Instead, you disobeyed the word of the Lord our God.
You grumbled in your tents, saying, “Because the Lord hated us, he brought us out of the land of Egypt to hand us over to the Amorites and destroy us.”

Where are we going up to? Your brothers discouraged you, saying, “We saw a great nation, numerous and stronger than we are, and great cities with walls built up to heaven. We also saw the descendants of the giants there.”
But I said to you, “Do not be alarmed or afraid of them.”
For the Lord our God goes ahead of you. He will help you fight against them, just as in all the deeds he did among you in the land of Egypt.
And in this wilderness, in what you have seen, the Lord your God cared for you as a man cares for his son, along the whole road you traveled until you reached this place.
And yet, in this matter, you did not trust the Lord our God,
who goes ahead of us on the road to choose a place for you, leading you at night with fire to show you the road you are to travel, and by day with a cloud.
And the Lord heard the sound of your words, and in his anger he swore, saying,
“None of these people will see this good land, concerning which I swore to their ancestors,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He will see it, and I will give him and his children the land he entered, because he follows the Lord.”
And the Lord was angry with me too because of you, saying, “You too will not enter that place.
Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, is the one who will enter it. Strengthen him, because he is the one who will give it to Israel as an inheritance.
And every young child who today does not know good or evil—they will enter it, and I will give it to them to inherit.
And you turned back and traveled through the wilderness along the road leading to the Red Sea.

And you answered me, saying, “We have sinned before the Lord our God. We will go up to fight against them, according to everything the Lord our God commanded us.” And each of you took his weapons of war, and you gathered together and went up the mountain.
And the Lord said to me, “Tell them, ‘Do not go up or fight against them, according to everything the Lord our God commanded us. I am not with you, lest you be crushed before your enemies.’”
I spoke to you, but you did not listen to me. You disobeyed the Lord’s command, forced your way ahead, and went up the mountain.
And the Amorites who lived on that mountain came out to fight against you. They chased you as swarms of bees do, and they struck you down from Seir as far as Hormah.
And you sat down and wept before the Lord, but the Lord did not listen to your voice or pay attention to you.
And you stayed in Kadesh for many days, according to the days you spent in that place.
Then we turned back and traveled into the wilderness along the road to the Red Sea, as the Lord had told me, and we went around Mount Seir for many days.
Then the Lord said to me,
“Stop going around this mountain. Now turn north.
And command the people, saying, ‘You will pass through the territory of your relatives, the descendants of Esau who live in Seir. They will fear you and tremble greatly.
Do not wage war against them, for I will not give you any of their land, not even enough to set a foot on, because I have given Mount Seir to the descendants of Esau as an inheritance.
You are to buy from them the food you will eat, and obtain measured amounts of water from them for money, so that you may drink it.

For the Lord our God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. Remember how you traveled through this vast, frightening wilderness. For forty years now, the Lord your God has been with you, and you have lacked nothing.’”

And we passed by our relatives, the descendants of Esau who live in Seir, along the Arabah road, from Elath and from Ezion-geber. Then we turned and passed along the road through the wilderness of Moab.

And the Lord said to me, “Do not act as an enemy toward the Moabites or wage war against them, for I will not give you any share of their land. For I have given Seir to the descendants of Lot for them to inherit.”
Those called Emim lived there formerly—a great nation, numerous and strong.
They too are counted as Rephaim, like the Anakim, and the Moabites call them Emim.

The Horites formerly lived in Seir, but the descendants of Esau destroyed them and drove them out before them, and settled in their place, just as Israel did in the land of its inheritance, which the Lord gave them.
Now then, get up, prepare yourselves, and let us cross the valley of Zered. And we crossed the valley of Zered.

The time from when we came out of Kadesh-barnea until we came out of the valley of Zered was thirty-eight years, until the whole generation of fighting men had perished from the camp, just as God had sworn to them.
God’s hand was against them, wiping them out of the camp until they had perished.
And it happened that, when all the fighting men had perished, having died from among the people,
the Lord spoke to me, saying:
For today you will pass through the territory of Moab, at Seir.

“When you approach the descendants of Ammon, do not act as their enemies or wage war against them. For I will not give you any of the land of the descendants of Ammon as an inheritance, because I have given it to the descendants of Lot as an inheritance.”
It is called the land of the Rephaim, for the Rephaim formerly lived there, and the Ammonites call them Zamzummim.
They were a great nation, numerous and very strong, like the Anakim. The Lord destroyed them before them, and they took possession of their land and settled in their place,
just as the descendants of Esau did to those who lived in Seir, destroying the Horites before them, taking possession of their land, and settling in their place to this day.
And the Hivites lived in Hazeroth as far as Gaza. The Cappadocians who came out of Cappadocia destroyed them and settled in their place.

“Now then, get up, prepare yourselves, and travel to the valley of Arnon. Look, I have handed over to you Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon, together with his land. Prepare to take possession of it, and wage war against him.
Today, begin to put fear and dread of you upon all the nations under heaven. When they hear your name, they will tremble, and anguish will seize them before you.”
I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying to him:
“Let me make my way through your land. I will travel only along the road; I will not turn to the right or to the left.
I will buy from you with my money the food I eat, and I will buy water from you to drink. Only let me travel through your land on foot,
just as the descendants of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Aroer did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land that the Lord our God will give us.”

But Sihon king of Heshbon was unwilling to let us pass through his territory, because the Lord our God had hardened his spirit and made his heart stubborn, so that he would be handed over to you today.
The Lord said to me, “Look, I have begun to hand over to you Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon, together with his land. Begin to take possession of his land.”
Sihon came out against us with all his people for battle at Jahaz.
The Lord our God handed him over to us, and we destroyed him, his sons, and all his people.
We took possession of all his cities at that time, and we destroyed all those cities, together with their women and children. We left no one alive.
But we took the livestock, and we took the plunder from the cities.
From Aroer, which lies beside the bank of the Arnon ravine, and the city in the valley, up to the hill country of Gilead, no city escaped us. The Lord our God handed all the cities over to us.
Except for the land of the Ammonites, which we did not approach: everything belonging to the Jabbok ravine and the cities in the hill country, as the Lord our God had commanded us concerning them.
Then we turned and went up the road leading to Bashan. Og king of Bashan came out with all his people to fight against us at Edrei.

The Lord said to me, “Do not be afraid of him, because I have handed him over to you, along with all his people and all his land. You will do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”
The Lord our God handed him over to us, along with Og king of Bashan and all his people. We struck him down and left none of his descendants behind.

We took possession of all his cities at that time. There was no city that we did not take from them: sixty cities, all those belonging to the region of Argob, which belonged to Og, the king in Bashan.
All the large cities were fortified with high walls, gates, and bars, apart from the very numerous cities of the Perizzites.
We destroyed them as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon. We destroyed all those cities, along with their women and their children.
We took all their livestock and the plunder from the cities for ourselves.
At that time we took the land from the two kings of the Amorites who lived on the other side of the Jordan, from the Arnon ravine up to Hermon.
The Phoenicians called Hermon Sirion, while the Amorites called it Senir.
All the cities of Mishor, all Gilead, and all Bashan, as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of Og’s kingdom in Bashan.

But the Rephaim had left Og king of Bashan behind. Look, his bed was an iron bed. It is in the territory of the Ammonites. Its length was nine cubits and its width four cubits, measured by a human cubit.
We took possession of that land at that time. From Aroer, which lies beside the bank of the Arnon ravine, and half the hill country of Gilead with its cities, I gave to Reuben and Gad.

The other half of the hill country of Gilead and all Bashan, which was Og’s kingdom, I gave to half the tribe of Manasseh. The whole region of Argob—all that Bashan—will be regarded as the land of the Rephaim.
Jair son of Manasseh took the whole region of Argob as far as the borders of the Girgashites and the Maacathites. He named it after himself: Bashan and [?] Jair, to this day.
And I gave Gilead to Machir.
To Reuben and Gad I gave the land from Gilead to the Arnon ravine, with the middle of the ravine as the boundary, and as far as the Jabbok ravine, which would be the boundary of the Ammonites.
The Arabah and the Jordan were the boundaries, from Chinnereth as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, from Ashedoth, the valley on the east.
At that time I commanded you, saying, “The Lord your God has given you this land as an inheritance. Arm yourselves and march ahead of your fellow Israelites, all you mighty men.”
But your wives, your children, and your livestock—I know that you have much livestock—are to stay in your cities, which I have given you,

until the Lord our God gives your brothers rest as he has given you, and they too take possession of the land that the Lord our God will give them on the other side of the Jordan. Then each of you will return to the inheritance that I have given you.”

And at that time I commanded Joshua, saying, “Your eyes have seen everything that the Lord our God did to these two kings. This is what the Lord will do to all the other kingdoms that you will cross over into.”
“Do not be afraid of them, because the Lord our God is the one who will fight against them for you.”
And at that time I pleaded with the Lord, saying,

“Lord, Lord, you have begun to show your servant your strength and your power, your mighty hand and your uplifted arm. For what other god is there in heaven or on earth who can act as you have acted and match your power?
Let me cross over, then, and see this good land on the other side of the Jordan, this good mountain and Anti-Lebanon.”
But the Lord disregarded me because of you and did not listen to me. The Lord said to me, “Enough! Do not speak about this matter again.
Go up to the top of the hewn mountain and lift your eyes toward the north, the west, the sea, and the east, and look, because you will not cross this Jordan.

Command Joshua, strengthen him, and encourage him, because he is the one who will cross over ahead of this people, and he is the one who will divide among them as an inheritance the land that you have seen.”
And we stayed in the valleys near Beth-peor.

Now, Israel, listen to the statutes and judgments that I am going to teach you today, so that you may carry them out, live, increase greatly, and enter and inherit the land that the Lord, the God of your ancestors, will give you.
You are to add to the word that I command you, and you must not take away from it, so that you may keep the commandments of the Lord our God that I will command you today.
Your eyes have seen everything that the Lord our God did concerning Baal-peor, because the Lord our God destroyed from among you everyone who followed Baal-peor.
But you who remain attached to the Lord our God are all alive today.
Take notice: I have taught you statutes and judgments, just as the Lord commanded us, so that we would carry them out [?] in the land that you are entering to inherit.

Keep them and carry them out, because this is your wisdom and your understanding before all the nations that will hear all these statutes. They will say, “Look, this great nation is a wise and learned people!”
For what other great nation has God as near to it as the Lord our God is in everything for which we call upon him?
And what other great nation has statutes and righteous judgments like this entire law that I will give you today?

Watch yourself and guard your soul carefully. Do not forget all the things that your eyes have seen, and do not let them leave your heart throughout all the days of your life. Teach them to your children and your children’s children,

concerning the day when you stood before the Lord your God at Horeb, on the day of the assembly, when the Lord said to me, “Gather your people together for me, so that they may hear my words and learn to fear me throughout all the days they spend on earth, and teach them to their children as well.”
And you approached and stood together at the foot of the mountain. The mountain was burning with fire up to heaven, and there was darkness, gloom, and a storm.
And the Lord spoke with you from the middle of the fire. You heard the sound of the words, but you did not see a form of God; you heard only a voice.
And he declared to you his covenant, which he commanded you to carry out—the ten words—and he wrote them on two stone tablets.
And at that time the Lord commanded me to teach you statutes and judgments for you to carry out in the land that you are entering to inherit.
And guard your souls very carefully, because you saw no form of the Lord on the day when he spoke with you at Horeb, on the mountain, from the midst of the fire.
Do not act lawlessly, and do not make yourselves a carved image in the likeness of any figure, the likeness of a man or a woman,
the likeness of any animal that lives on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird that flies beneath the sky,
the likeness of any creeping creature that moves on the earth, the likeness of any fish that moves in the waters beneath the earth.

And do not lift your eyes to the sky and see the sun, the moon, the stars, and the whole array of heaven, and be led astray into worshiping them and serving them. These are what the Lord your God has allotted to all the nations beneath heaven.
But God took you and brought you out of the iron furnace, which is the land of Egypt, to become his own people, as you are today.
And the Lord was angry with me because of the words you were saying, and he swore that I would not cross this Jordan and would not enter the land that the Lord will give you as an inheritance.
For I will die in this land and will not cross this Jordan. But you will cross it and inherit the good land.

Be careful not to forget the covenant of the Lord our God, which he established with you, and make yourselves a carved image in the likeness of any of the things about which the Lord your God commanded you.
For the Lord your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.

When you have children, and your children have children, and you have lived a long time in the land, and you act lawlessly and make yourselves a carved image in the likeness of any of these things, and do evil in the sight of the Lord your God to provoke him to anger,

then today I call heaven and earth to witness against you that you will be utterly destroyed from the land that you are crossing the Jordan to enter and inherit. You will spend a long time on it, but you will be utterly wiped out.
And the Lord will scatter you among all the nations, and you will be left few in number among the nations into which the Lord God will bring you.
And there you will serve other gods, objects made by human hands from wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or eat or smell.
And in that place you will seek the Lord your God and not find him, if you seek him with all your heart and all your soul in your distress.
And all these things will overtake you in the last days, and you will return to the Lord your God and obey his voice.
For the Lord your God is a merciful God. He will not abandon you or destroy you, nor will he forget the covenant with your ancestors, which he swore to them.

Ask about the former days that came before you, from the day when God created humanity on the earth, and from one end of heaven to the other: has anything like this great event ever happened, or has anything like it ever been heard of?
Has a nation ever heard the voice of the living God speaking from the midst of the fire, as you heard it, and lived?

Has God ever attempted to go and take for himself a nation from the midst of another nation, through trials, signs, wonders, war, a mighty hand, an uplifted arm, and great visions, like everything the Lord your God did in Egypt, [?] before your eyes?
This was so that you would know that the Lord your God is God, and there is no other besides him.
He made you hear his voice from heaven to instruct you, and on earth he made you see his great fire, and you heard his words from the midst of the fire.
Because he loved your ancestors and chose their descendants after them—that is, you—he himself brought you out of Egypt by his great power,
to drive out before you great nations stronger than you, to bring you into their land and give it to you as an inheritance, as you possess it today.
And today you must understand and consider in your heart that the Lord your God is the one in heaven above and on the earth below. There is no other besides him.

And you shall keep his statutes and his commandments, which I command you today, so that things may go well for you and your children after you, and so that you may live many days in the land that the Lord your God will give you forever.
Then Moses set apart three cities on the other side of the Jordan, toward the sunrise.
So that the killer who kills his neighbor unintentionally, without having hated him before, may flee to them. He shall flee to one of these cities and live.
They are Bezer in the wilderness, in the land in the plain, belonging to Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead, belonging to Gad; and Golan in Bashan, belonging to Manasseh.
This is the law that Moses set before the Israelites.
These are the testimonies, statutes, and judgments that Moses proclaimed to the Israelites in the wilderness when they came out of the land of Egypt,

on the other side of the Jordan, in the valley near Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon. Moses and the Israelites defeated them when they came out of the land of Egypt.
And they took possession of his land and the land of Og, king of Bashan—the two kings of the Amorites who were on the other side of the Jordan, toward the sunrise.
From Aroer, which is on the bank of the Arnon ravine, to Mount Sion, which is Hermon.
The whole Arabah and the other side of the Jordan toward the sunrise, from Ashdoth, which is [?].
Moses summoned all Israel and said to them, “Listen, Israel, to the statutes and judgments that I will proclaim in your hearing today, so that you may learn them and be careful to carry them out.”
The Lord our God made a covenant with you at Horeb.
The Lord did not make this covenant with your fathers, but he made it with you, all of you who are alive here today.
The Lord spoke with you face to face on the mountain, from the midst of the fire.
I myself was standing between the Lord and you at that time to proclaim the Lord's words to you, because you were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain. He said:
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of your slavery.
You shall have no other gods before me.
You shall not make a carved image for yourself, or any likeness of anything in heaven above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath the earth.

You shall not bow down to them or serve them, because I am the Lord your God, a jealous God, who punishes the children for the sins of their fathers, to the third and fourth generations of those who hate me.
And I show mercy to a thousand generations of those who love me and keep my commandments.
You shall not use the name of the Lord your God for a worthless purpose, for the Lord will not forgive anyone who uses his name for a worthless purpose.
Observe the Sabbath day and keep it holy, as the Lord your God commanded you.
You shall spend six days working and do all your work during them.

But the seventh day is a Sabbath to the Lord your God. You must not do any work on it—you, your son, your daughter, your male slave, your female slave, your ox, your donkey, any of your livestock, or the foreign resident within your gates—so that your slave may rest just as you do.

And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God brought you out of that place with a mighty hand and an uplifted arm. Therefore the Lord your God commanded you to observe the Sabbath day and keep it holy.
Honor your father and your mother, as the Lord your God commanded you, so that things may go well for you and so that you may live a long time in the land that the Lord your God will give you.
You shall not commit adultery.
You shall not murder.
You must not steal.
You must not testify falsely against your neighbor by giving false testimony.

You must not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor must you covet your neighbor’s house, his field, his male slave, his female slave, his ox, his donkey, any animal belonging to him, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.

These are the words that the Lord spoke to your entire assembly on the mountain, from the midst of the fire, amid darkness, a cloud, a storm, and a voice. He said no more. He wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
And when you heard the voice from the midst of the fire, while the mountain was ablaze, you came to me—the leaders of your tribes and your elders.

You said to me, “Look, the Lord our God has shown us his glory, and we have heard his voice from the midst of the fire. Today we have seen that God can speak with a human being and that person can remain alive.
Now then, must we die and be destroyed by this great fire? If we continue to hear the voice of the Lord our God again, we will die.
For what mortal, or who, has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the midst of the fire as we have, and remained alive?
You yourself must go near and hear what the Lord our God will say to you. Then tell us everything that the Lord our God says to you, and we will listen and do it.”
The Lord heard the sound of your words as you spoke them to me. The Lord said to me, “I have heard the words that these people have spoken to you. Everything they have said is good.
Who will make their hearts remain like this within them, so that they fear me and keep my commandments all their days, so that things may go well with them and their children forever?
Go and tell them, ‘Return to your dwellings.’

But you must stand here with me, so that I may tell you the commandments, statutes, and judgments that you are to teach them, so that they may carry them out in the land that I will give them as an inheritance.”
You must be careful to act as the Lord your God has commanded you. You must not turn to the right or to the left.

Instead, follow the whole path that the Lord your God has commanded you to walk, so that he may give you rest, things may go well for you, and you may live many days in the land that you will inherit.
These are the commandments and statutes that the Lord our God commanded me to teach you, so that you may carry them out in the land that you are entering to inherit.

So that you may fear the Lord our God, keeping all his statutes and commandments that I am giving you today—you, your children, and your children’s children, throughout all the days of their lives—and so that you may live many days.

Listen, then, Israel, and be careful to carry them out, so that things may go well for you and you may increase greatly, just as the Lord, the God of your ancestors, promised you, to give you a land flowing with milk and honey.
These are the statutes and judgments that Moses commanded the Israelites in the wilderness when they came out of the land of Egypt. Listen, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
You must love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your mind, all your soul, and all your strength.
And let these words that I command you today be in your heart and in your soul,
so that you teach them to your children and speak about them when you sit in your house, when you walk along the road, when you are on your beds, and when you get up.
You must also write them as a sign on your hand, and they must be fixed before your eyes.
You must write them on the doorposts of your houses and inside your dwellings.
And when the Lord your God brings you into the land concerning which the Lord your God swore to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give you great and good cities that you did not build,
Houses filled with every good thing that you did not fill, wells dug that you did not dig, and vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant—and when you eat and are satisfied,
be careful not to forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of your slavery.
You must fear the Lord your God and serve him alone. You must cling to [?] and swear by his name.
You must not go after other gods, any of the gods of the nations around you,
because the Lord your God, who is among you, is a jealous God. Otherwise the Lord your God may turn against you in anger and destroy you from the face of the earth.
Do not put the Lord your God to the test as you tested him in the testing.
Carefully keep the commandments of the Lord your God, his testimonies, and his statutes, which he commanded you to keep.
And do what is pleasing and good before the Lord your God, so that things may go well with you and you may enter and inherit the good land about which he swore to your ancestors,
so that he may drive out all your enemies before you, just as he said.
And when your son asks you in the future, saying, “What are these testimonies, statutes, and judgments that the Lord our God commanded us to keep?”
you shall tell your son, “We were Pharaoh’s slaves in the land of Egypt, and the Lord brought us out of there with a strong hand and an uplifted arm.
And before our eyes the Lord performed signs and great, terrible wonders in the land of Egypt, against Pharaoh and his household.
But he brought us out of there to bring us in and give us this land, which he swore to give to our ancestors.
And the Lord commanded us to carry out all these statutes and to fear the Lord our God, so that things might go well with us always and we might live, as we do today.
And mercy will be shown to us if we take care to carry out all these commandments before the Lord our God, just as the Lord commanded us.”

When the Lord your God brings you into the land that you are entering to inherit, and removes from before you great and numerous nations—the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, seven nations more numerous and stronger than you—
and the Lord your God delivers them into your hands, you shall strike them and utterly destroy them. Do not make a covenant with them or show them mercy.
You must not give your daughter to his son, and you must not take his daughter for your son.
For she will turn your son away from me, and he will serve other gods. Then the Lord will become angry with you and quickly destroy you.
Instead, this is what you shall do to them: tear down their altars, break their pillars, cut down their sacred groves, and burn the carved images of their gods with fire.
For you are a people holy to the Lord your God, and the Lord your God chose you to be a people honored by him above all the nations on the face of the earth.
It was not because you were not far more numerous than all the nations that the Lord loved you and chose you, for you are fewer in number than the other nations.

Rather, because the Lord loves you and keeps the oath he swore to your ancestors, the Lord brought you out with a strong hand and an uplifted arm. He redeemed you from the house of your slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
And you shall know that the Lord your God is God, the faithful God who keeps his covenant and his mercy for those who love him and keep his commandments, for a thousand generations.
And he repays those who hate him, wiping them out before him. He will not delay in repaying those who hate him.
And you shall keep these commandments, statutes, and judgments that I command you today to carry out.
And if you listen to all these statutes, keep them, and carry them out, the Lord your God will keep his covenant and his mercy for you, just as he swore to your ancestors.

And he will love you, bless you, and increase your numbers. He will bless your offspring and the produce of your land—your grain, your wine, and your oil—and the herds of your cattle and the flocks of your sheep, in the land about which the Lord swore to your ancestors, “I will give it to you.”
And you will be blessed above all the nations. There will be no childlessness or barrenness among you or among your livestock.

And the Lord will remove from you every sickness and every infirmity, along with the terrible plagues of Egypt that you saw and knew. He will not bring them upon you, but he will bring them upon all your enemies and everyone who hates you.
And you will consume all the spoils of the nations that the Lord your God will give you. Do not look on them with pity, and do not worship their gods, for this is a snare and an abomination.
But if you say in your heart, “This nation is more numerous than I am. How will I destroy it?”
Do not be afraid of them. Be sure to remember what the Lord your God did to Pharaoh and all the Egyptians:

the great trials that your eyes saw, these signs and these great wonders, and the strong hand and the uplifted arm with which the Lord your God brought you out. This is what the Lord our God will do to all the other nations that you fear.
And the Lord your God will send hornets among them until those who remain and those who have hidden from you become weak.
You will not tremble before them, because the Lord your God is with you, a great and mighty God.

And the Lord your God will destroy these nations before you little by little. You will not be able to destroy them immediately, so that the land does not become deserted around you and the wild animals multiply against you.
The Lord your God will hand them over to you and inflict great destruction on them until he has wiped them out.
And he will hand their kings over to you, and you will erase their names from that place. No one will stand against you until you have destroyed them.

You must burn the carved images of their gods in a fire. Do not desire any silver or gold from them, and do not take any of it for yourself, lest you sin because of it. It is an abomination to the Lord your God.
Therefore, you must not bring a detestable thing into your house, lest you too become detestable like it. You must utterly hate it and utterly detest it, because it is defiled.
You must carefully carry out all the commandments that I give you today, so that you may live and multiply greatly, and enter and inherit the land concerning which the Lord swore to your ancestors.

And you must remember the whole journey on which the Lord your God made you travel in the wilderness—this is the fortieth year—to afflict you and test you, so that what is in your heart might be revealed: whether you would keep his commandments or not.

And he humbled you and left you hungry, and then fed you with manna, which your ancestors did not know, to teach you that a person will not live on bread alone, but will live on every word that comes from the mouth of God.
Your clothes did not wear out on you, and your feet did not swell during these forty years.
And you must understand in your heart that just as a man disciplines his son, so the Lord your God will discipline you.
And you must keep the commandments of the Lord your God, walking in his ways and fearing him.
For the Lord your God will bring you into a good and spacious land, a place with streams of water and abundant springs of water flowing through the fields and the mountains,
a land of wheat and barley, vineyards, fig trees, and pomegranate trees, a land of olives, oil, and honey,
a land where you will not eat your bread in poverty and will lack nothing, a land whose stones are like iron and from whose mountains you will mine copper.
And you will eat and be satisfied, and bless the Lord your God for the good land that the Lord your God has given you.
Be careful not to forget the Lord your God by failing to keep his commandments, his judgments, and his statutes, which I command you to observe,
lest, when you eat and are satisfied, and build good and beautiful houses and live in them,
and your sheep and cattle multiply, and your silver and gold increase, and everything you possess increases,
you become proud in your heart and forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of your slavery.

The one who led you through the great and terrifying wilderness, where there were burning snakes, scorpions, and thirst, and where there was no water; the one who brought you a spring of water from hard rock.
The one who fed you manna in the wilderness, which your ancestors did not know, so that he might humble you and test you, and afterward do you good in the end.
And do not say in your heart, “My strength and the power of my hands have produced this great wealth for me.”
Instead, remember the Lord your God, for he is the one who strengthens you to acquire wealth, so that he may establish his covenant, which the Lord swore to your ancestors, as it is today.
But if you completely forget the Lord your God and follow other, foreign gods, serve them, and worship them, I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that you will certainly perish.
Like the other nations that the Lord God will destroy before you, you too will perish, because you did not obey the voice of the Lord your God.
Listen, Israel: today you are about to cross the Jordan to enter and take possession of great nations much stronger than you, and great cities fortified with walls reaching up to the sky.
A great people, numerous and tall, the descendants of Anak, whom you know and about whom you have heard it said, “Who can stand against the descendants of Anak?”

And understand today that the Lord your God is the one who goes before you as a consuming fire. He is the one who will drive them out, and he is the one who will crush them before you. He will drive them out and destroy them immediately, just as the Lord told you.

And when the Lord your God wipes out all these nations before you, do not say in your heart, “It is because of my righteousness that the Lord has brought me in to inherit this good land.” Rather, it is because of the wickedness of these nations that the Lord will destroy them before you.

It is not because of your righteousness or the purity of your heart that you will enter their land and take possession of it. Rather, it is because of the wickedness of these nations that the Lord will drive them out before you, and so that he may establish his covenant, which the Lord swore to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
And understand today that it is not because of your righteousness that the Lord your God will give you this good land to possess, for you are a stubborn people.

Remember, and do not forget, the deeds by which you provoked the Lord your God in the wilderness. From the day you came out of the land of Egypt until you arrived at this place, you continued to disobey the Lord.
At Horeb too, you provoked the Lord, and the Lord became angry with you, ready to destroy you.

When I went up the mountain to receive the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant that the Lord established with you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights, without eating bread or drinking water.
And the Lord gave me the two stone tablets, written with the finger of God. Written on them were all the words that the Lord spoke to you on the mountain on the day you gathered together.
And after forty days and forty nights, the Lord gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.

And the Lord said to me, “Get up and go down quickly from here, for your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, have acted wickedly. They have immediately turned aside from the way you commanded them to follow. They have made themselves a cast-metal god.”
And the Lord said to me, “I have spoken to you once and twice, saying, ‘I have seen this people, and look, they are a stubborn people.’
Leave me alone, so that I may destroy them and erase their name from under heaven, and make you into a great nation, stronger and far more numerous than this one.”
And when I turned back, I came down the mountain. The mountain was burning with fire, and the two tablets were in my hands.
And when I saw that you had sinned before the Lord your God, and had made yourselves a cast-metal god, and had abandoned the way that the Lord had commanded you to follow,
I took hold of the two stone tablets, threw them out of my hands, and shattered them before your eyes.

And I prayed before the Lord a second time for forty days and forty nights, without eating bread or drinking water. I prayed over all the sins you had committed, doing evil before the Lord your God and provoking him to anger.
And I was afraid because of the anger and wrath with which the Lord was furious with you, intending to destroy you. But the Lord listened to me again at that time.
The Lord was also very angry with Aaron and intended to destroy him. And I also prayed for Aaron at that time.

And I took the sinful thing you had made—the calf—and burned it in fire. I broke it into tiny pieces until it was very fine, making it like dust, and threw the dust into the stream flowing down from the mountain.
And at the Burning and the Testing and at the Memorials of Desire, you were provoking the Lord your God to anger.

And when the Lord sent you out from Kadesh-barnea, saying to you, “Go up and take possession of the land that I will give you,” you did not obey the word of the Lord your God. You did not believe him or listen to his voice.
You have been unfaithful to the Lord since the day he revealed himself to you.
And I prayed before the Lord for forty days and forty nights, which I spent praying, because the Lord had said that he would destroy you.

And I prayed to God, saying, “Lord, Lord, king of the gods, do not destroy your people and your inheritance, whom you redeemed by your power, by your mighty hand, and by your uplifted arm, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt.”
Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself. Do not be angry over this people's fault, their wickedness, and their sins.

Otherwise, those who live in the land from which you brought us out might say, “Because the Lord could not bring them into the land he had spoken to them about, and because the Lord hated them, he brought them out to kill them in this wilderness.”
And these are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt by your great power and your uplifted arm.
At that time the Lord said to me, “Carve out for yourself two stone tablets like the first ones, and come up to me on the mountain. Also make yourself a wooden chest.
For I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke, and you are to put them into the chest.”
And I made the chest from wood that does not decay, and carved out the two stone tablets like the first ones. I went up the mountain, with the two tablets in my hands.
And he wrote on the tablets, as in the first inscription, the ten words that the Lord had spoken to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire. And the Lord gave them to me.
I turned and came down from the mountain, and put the tablets into the chest that I had made. And they were in it, just as the Lord had commanded me.
The Israelites set out from Beeroth of the sons of Jaakim to Misadai. Aaron died there and was buried there, and his son Eleazar succeeded him as priest.
They moved on from that place and came to Gadtag, and from Gadgad to Jotbathah, a stream of water.
At that time the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the chest of the Lord's covenant, to stand before the Lord serving him and praying in his name, down to this day.
For this reason the Levites have no share or inheritance among their brothers. The Lord himself is their inheritance, just as he told them.
But I remained on the mountain for forty days and forty nights. And the Lord listened to me at that time; the Lord did not wish to destroy you.
And the Lord said to me, “Go and lead this people, so that they may enter and take possession of the land that I swore to their fathers I would give them.”
Now, Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you except to fear the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, to love him, and to serve the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul?
and to keep the commandments of the Lord your God and his statutes, which I am commanding you today, so that things may go well for you?
Look, heaven belongs to the Lord your God, as do the heaven of heavens and the earth, with everything in them.
Yet the Lord chose your ancestors to love them, and he chose their descendants after them—that is, you—above all the nations, as is the case today.
Circumcise your hard hearts, and do not remain stiff-necked any longer.
For the Lord your God is the God of gods and the Lord of lords, the great God, alone, mighty and fearsome, who shows no favoritism and will not accept a bribe.
He provides justice for the poor, the orphan, and the widow, and he loves the foreign resident, giving him bread and clothing.
You must also love the foreign resident, for you yourselves were foreign residents in the land of Egypt.
Fear the Lord your God, serve him alone, hold fast to him, and swear by his name.
He is your pride, and he is your God, who performed these great wonders for you, which your own eyes saw.
For your ancestors went down to Egypt as seventy people, but now the Lord your God has made them as numerous as the stars of heaven.
And you shall love the Lord your God and keep his instructions, which he commanded you, and his statutes, his commandments, and his judgments, throughout all your days.

You must understand today that the Lord did not do these things with your children, who do not know and have not seen the instruction of the Lord your God, his great deeds, his mighty hand, and his uplifted arm,
and his signs and wonders that he performed in the midst of Egypt against Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and all his land,

and the other deeds that he performed by his power against the Egyptians, their chariots, and their horses: how the water of the Red Sea covered them as they pursued us from behind, and the Lord killed them, to this very day,
and the other deeds that he performed for you in the wilderness until you came to this place,

And the other things he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab son of Reuben: how the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their homes, their tents, and everything they owned, in the midst of all Israel.
For your own eyes saw all the great deeds of the Lord that he performed for you today.

You must keep all his commandments that I am giving you today, so that you may live and increase greatly, and enter and take possession of the land that you are going to cross the Jordan to enter and possess,
so that you may live many days on the land that the Lord swore to your ancestors to give to them and their descendants after them—a land flowing with milk and honey.
For the land that you are going to enter and possess is not like the land of Egypt, from which you came, where people sow seed and water it with hard work, like a vegetable garden [?].
Instead, the land that you are going to enter and possess is a land of hills and valleys, drinking water from the rain.

It is a land that the Lord your God cares for at all times. The eyes of the Lord your God watch over it at all times; the eyes of the Lord your God watch over it from the beginning of the year to the end of the year.
If you faithfully obey all his commandments that I am giving you today, loving the Lord your God and serving him with all your heart and all your soul,
I will give rain to your land at its proper time, the early rain and the late rain, and you will gather your grain, your wine, and your oil.
And he will provide food for your livestock in your fields.
When you have eaten and are satisfied, be on your guard. Do not let your heart be led astray, so that you turn away and serve other gods and worship them.

Otherwise, the Lord will blaze with anger against you and shut the sky so that you have no rain, and the land will not yield its produce, and you will quickly perish from the good land that the Lord has given you.
You must place these words in your heart and in your soul, and bind them as a sign on your hands, and let them be fastened before your eyes.
Teach them to your children, so that they speak about them when they sit in their homes, when they walk along the road, when they lie down, and when they get up.
Write them on the doorposts of your houses and at the entrances to your dwellings.
So that you may live many days, and your children's days may multiply on the land that the Lord swore to your ancestors to give you, like the days of the heavens over the earth.
But if you obey all these commandments that I am commanding you today, carrying them out, loving the Lord our God, walking in all his commandments, and holding fast to him,
Then the Lord will drive out all these nations before you, and you will take possession of great nations much stronger than you.

Every place where the soles of your feet tread will belong to you. Your borders will extend from the wilderness and Anti-Lebanon, and from the river, the great river Euphrates, as far as the sea toward the west.
No one will stand against you. The Lord your God will put fear and dread of you throughout the whole land that you are entering, just as the Lord told you.
Look, today I am setting blessings and curses before you.
The blessing, if you obey the commandments of the Lord your God that I am giving you today;

But the curses, if you do not obey the commandments of the Lord your God that I am giving you, and you stray from the path that I commanded you to follow, going to worship other gods whom you do not know.
When the Lord your God brings you into the land that you are crossing into to take possession of it, you must pronounce the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
Look, they are on the other side of the Jordan, beyond the road leading toward the sunset, in the land of Canaan that lies to the west, near Gilgal, beside the tall tree.
For you will cross the Jordan and enter to take possession of the land that the Lord your God will give you as an inheritance for all your days, and you will live on it.
Be careful to carry out all these ordinances and laws that I am commanding you today.
These are the ordinances and laws that you must carefully carry out in the land that the Lord, the God of your ancestors, will give you as an inheritance, for all the days that you live on the earth.

You must completely destroy all the places where the nations you are going to dispossess worshiped their gods, where they offer sacrifices on the high mountains, on the seashores, and under shady trees.
You must demolish their altars, break their pillars, burn their groves, and burn the carved images of their gods with fire. Erase their names from that place.
You must not do these things to the Lord your God.
Instead, seek out the place that the Lord your God will choose in one of your tribes, where his name is to be proclaimed and he is to be called upon, and go there.
And bring there your burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your firstfruits, your tithes, your vowed offerings, and the firstborn of your cattle and sheep.
Eat there before the Lord your God, and rejoice in all the work you undertake, you and your children, because the Lord your God has blessed you.
You must not do everything that you are doing here today, each person doing what seems pleasing in their own eyes.
For you have not yet entered your place of rest and the inheritance that the Lord your God will give you.
You will cross the Jordan and live in the land that the Lord your God will give you as an inheritance. He will give you rest from all your enemies around you, and you will live in safety.

Then, at the place that the Lord your God will choose for his name to be proclaimed there, you must bring everything that I am commanding you today: your burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your tithes, the firstfruits of your hands, and all your choice gifts that you vow to our God.

You shall rejoice in the presence, in the presence of the Lord your God—you, your sons and daughters, your male and female slaves, and the Levite within your gates, because he has no share or inheritance among you.
Be careful not to raise your hands in every place you see.
Instead, in the place that the Lord your God will choose in one of your cities, you shall offer your burnt offerings. There you shall do everything that I command you today.

But whenever you wish, you may slaughter and eat meat, as much as you desire, according to the blessing that the Lord your God has given you, in all your cities. The unclean person with you and the clean person may eat together, just as they eat a gazelle or a deer.
However, you must not eat the blood. Instead, you shall pour it out on the ground like water.

You must not eat in any of your cities the tithe of your grain, wine, and oil, the firstborn of your cattle and sheep, any of the offerings you vow to give, your freewill offerings, or the firstfruits of your hands.

Instead, you shall eat them before the Lord your God in the place that the Lord your God will choose for himself—you, your son and daughter, your male and female slaves, and the foreign resident in your cities. You shall rejoice before the Lord your God, you and your son and daughter, over everything you undertake.
Be careful not to neglect the Levite for as long as you live on the earth.
When the Lord your God enlarges your territory, as he has told you, and you say, “I will eat meat,” because you desire meat, you may eat meat as much as you desire.

If the place that the Lord your God has chosen for his name to be proclaimed there is far from you, you may slaughter some of your cattle and sheep that the Lord your God will give you, in the way that I have commanded you, and eat in your cities as much as you desire.
Just as a gazelle and a deer are eaten, so you shall eat them. The unclean person with you and the clean person may eat these.
Be very careful not to eat blood, because the blood is its life. Therefore, you must not eat the life with the meat.
You must not eat it; you shall pour it out on the ground like water.
You must not eat it, so that things may go well for you and your children after you, when you do what is good and pleasing to the Lord your God.

However, you shall take the offerings you have vowed to give and the sacred things that belong to you, and go up to the place that the Lord your God will choose for himself, so that his name may be invoked there.
You shall prepare your burnt offerings for him and offer them on the altar of the Lord your God, but you may eat the meat.

Observe, listen to, and carry out all these words that I command you today, so that things may go well for you and your children forever, when you do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
But when the Lord your God destroys all the nations whose land you are entering to possess, and you take possession of them and settle in their land,

Be careful not to pursue them as though caught in a snare, after you have destroyed them from before you. Do not inquire about their gods, saying, “How do these nations serve their gods, so that I may do the same?”
You must not do these things to the Lord your God, for they have done for their gods the abominations that the Lord hates. They even burn their sons and daughters in the fire for their gods.
Every command that I give you today you shall be careful to carry out. You must not add to it or take away from it.
If a prophet or a dream interpreter arises among you and gives you a sign or a wonder,
and the sign and the wonder that he told you about come to pass, while he says, “Let us go, and you shall serve other gods whom you have not known,”
You must not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer, for the Lord your God is testing you to reveal whether you love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
you shall follow the Lord your God, and it is he whom you shall fear. You shall keep his commandments and obey his voice.

And that prophet or dreamer shall die, because he spoke to lead you astray from the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from your slavery. He wanted to drive you away from the path that the Lord your God commanded you to follow. You shall remove the evil person from among you.

But if your brother, from the same father or the same mother, or your son or daughter, or your wife who is with you, or your friend who is close to your heart, urges you secretly, saying, “Let us go, and you can serve other gods,” whom neither you nor your ancestors have known,
From among the gods of the nations around you, those near you and those far from you, from one end of the earth to the other.
you must not agree with him or listen to him. Your eye must not pity him, and you must not love him or conceal what he has done.
You must certainly report him to them. Your hands shall be the first against him to kill him, and afterward the hands of all the people shall be against him.
They shall stone him to death with stones, because he sought a way to lead you away from the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of your slavery.
When all Israel hears, they will be afraid and will no longer do such an evil thing among you.
But if you hear people saying in one of your cities that the Lord your God will give you to live in,
“Lawless people have come out from among us and have led astray all those who live in their cities, saying to them, ‘Let us go and serve other gods,’ whom you have not known,”
you shall rise and inquire and investigate very carefully. And if the report is indeed true, and this detestable thing has happened among you,
you must certainly kill everyone living in that city with the sword. You shall utterly destroy it along with everyone living in it.

You shall gather all its plunder into its streets and burn the city with fire, along with all its plunder and everything in it, before the Lord your God. It shall remain deserted forever, and they must never rebuild it.

Nothing from what is devoted to destruction shall cling to your hands, so that the Lord may turn away from his fierce anger, grant you mercy, have compassion on you, and multiply you, as the Lord swore to your ancestors,
if you truly obey the voice of the Lord your God, keeping all his commandments that I command you today, and doing what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
You are children of the Lord your God. You must not cut yourselves or shave yourselves bald for someone who has died.
For you are a people holy to the Lord your God, and the Lord your God has chosen you to be his chosen people out of all the nations on the face of the earth.
You must not eat anything detestable.
These are the animals you may eat: a calf from your cattle, a lamb from your sheep, and a young goat from the goats;
a deer, a gazelle, a wild ox, a goat-antelope, a white-rumped antelope, and a giraffe.
And any animal whose foot is divided into split hooves and that chews the cud—these are the animals you may eat.

But these you must not eat among those that chew the cud and whose hooves are not split: the camel, the hare, and the rock hyrax. Because they chew the cud but their hooves are not split on their feet, these are unclean for you.
And you must not eat the pig, because although its hooves are split on its foot, it does not chew the cud. It is unclean for you. You must not eat its flesh, and you must not touch their dead bodies.
And these you may eat from all that live in the waters: any fish that has fins and scales you may eat.
But any fish that has neither fins nor scales you must not eat. These are unclean for you.
You may eat every clean bird.
And these are the ones among them that you must not eat: the eagle, the vulture, and the osprey,
And the vulture and the [?], and those like them.
and the raven and those like it.
And the ostrich, the owl, and the gull,
and the cormorant, and the hawk and others of its kind,
and the hoopoe and the night raven,
and the pelican, the plover and others of its kind, and the purple swamphen and the bat.
All these birds are unclean for you. You must not eat any of them.
You may eat any clean bird.

And you must not eat anything unclean. Animals that have died are to be given to the foreigner living in your towns, so that he may eat them, or you may give them to someone you do not know, because you are a people holy to the Lord your God. You must not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.
You must give a tenth of all the produce of your seed, the produce of your field, year by year.

And you must eat it before the Lord your God in the place that the Lord your God will choose for himself, where his name is to be invoked. You must bring to that place a tenth of your grain, your wine, and your oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and sheep, so that you may learn to fear the Lord your God all your days.

But if the journey is too long for them, and you cannot carry them to that place because the place that the Lord your God will choose, where his name is to be proclaimed, is far from you, because the Lord your God has blessed you,
you must sell it for money, take the money in your hands, and go up to the place that the Lord your God will choose.

And you must spend the money on whatever you desire: cattle, sheep, wine, strong drink, or anything else you desire. He shall eat it there before the Lord your God, and you and your son shall rejoice.
And the Levite who lives in your towns, because he has no share or inheritance with you.
After three years, you must bring out the entire tenth of your produce for that year and store it in your towns.

And the Levite shall come, because he has no share or inheritance with you, along with the resident foreigner, the orphan, and the widow who live in your towns. They shall eat and be satisfied, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the work you do.
Every seven years, you must cancel debts.

And this is the rule for canceling debts: you must cancel every written claim for money that you hold against your neighbor. You must not demand payment from your brother, because cancellation has been proclaimed by the Lord your God.
You may demand from a foreigner what he owes you, but you must cancel what your brother owes you.
So there shall be no needy person among you, because on account of this the Lord your God will bless you in the land that he will give you as an inheritance for you to possess,
if you truly obey the voice of the Lord your God, keeping and carrying out all his commandments that I command you today.

For the Lord your God has blessed you, just as he told you. You shall lend at interest to many nations, but you yourself shall not borrow at interest. You shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you.

But if one of your brothers becomes needy among you, in one of your towns in the land that the Lord your God will give you, you must not turn your heart away from him or close your hand to your brother or to the needy person.
You shall freely open your hand to him and lend him whatever he needs, according to his lack.

So be careful: do not let a secret thought arise in your heart, a lawless thought, saying, ‘The seventh year, the year of debt cancellation, is near,’ so that you look unkindly on your needy brother and give him nothing. He may cry out to the Lord against you, and it will become a great sin for you.

Instead, you shall freely give to him and freely lend him whatever he needs. Your heart must not be grieved when you give to him, because on account of this the Lord your God will bless you in all your work and in everything you undertake.
For needy people will never disappear from the land. Therefore I give you this command: you must open your hand generously to your poor brother and to the needy person in your land.
But if your fellow Hebrew, a man or a woman, is sold to you, he shall serve you for six years. In the seventh year, you must send him away from you free.
But when you send him away from you as a free man, you must not send him away empty-handed.
You must generously give him enough from your sheep, your grain, and your winepress. You must give to him according to how the Lord your God has blessed you.
And you must remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God redeemed you from there. Therefore I command you to do this.
But if he says to you, “I will not leave you, because I love you and your household, because he is comfortable with you,”
you must take an awl and pierce his ear at the door, and he will be your slave forever. You must do the same for your female slave.

You must not consider it a hardship when they leave you as free people, because he has served you as a slave for six years, like a hired worker hired by the year. And the Lord your God will bless you in everything you do.
You must consecrate to the Lord your God every male firstborn born to you among your cattle and sheep. You must not work with your firstborn calf, and you must not shear the firstborn of your sheep.
Instead, you and your household must eat it before the Lord your God, year after year, in the place that the Lord your God will choose for himself.
But if it has a defect, if it is lame or blind or has any other serious defect, you must not offer it as a sacrifice to the Lord your God.
Instead, you must eat it in your towns. Both the unclean person who is with you and the clean person may eat these things, just as they eat a gazelle or a deer.
But you must not eat its blood. You must pour it onto the ground like water.
In the month of new crops, celebrate the Passover to the Lord your God, because in this month of new crops you came out of the land of Egypt by night.
You must sacrifice sheep and cattle as the Passover offering to the Lord your God in the place that the Lord your God will choose for himself, so that his name may be proclaimed there.

You must not eat leavened bread there. For seven days you must eat unleavened bread, the bread of hardship, because you came out of the land of Egypt in haste, so that you may remember the day you came out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life.
There must be no leaven with you anywhere within your borders, and none of the meat that you slaughter on the evening of the first day must be left until morning.
You may not sacrifice the Passover offering in any of your towns that the Lord God will give you.

Instead, in the place that the Lord your God will choose for himself, so that his name may be proclaimed there, you must sacrifice the Passover offering in the evening, at sunset, at the time when you came out of the land of Egypt.
And you shall boil it, roast it, and eat it in the place that the Lord your God will choose. In the morning you shall turn back and go to your own place.

For six days you must eat unleavened bread, and the seventh day, on which you came out, is the word of the Lord your God [?]. You must not do any work on it except the tasks necessary for your own needs.
You must count seven weeks for yourself. From the time you begin to harvest, this is how you must count the seven weeks.
Then celebrate the Festival of Weeks to the Lord your God according to what you can afford, from what he will give you, according to the blessing with which the Lord your God has blessed you.

And you must rejoice before the Lord your God—you, your son, your daughter, your male slave, your female slave, the Levite in your towns, and the foreign resident, the orphan, and the widow who are among you—in the place that the Lord your God will choose for himself, so that his name may be proclaimed there.
And you must remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and you must be careful to carry out all these commands.
You must celebrate the Festival of Shelters for seven days when you gather in your produce and what comes from your winepress.
And you must rejoice at your festival—you, your son, your daughter, your male slave, your female slave, the Levite, the foreign resident, the orphan, and the widow who are in your towns.

For seven days you shall celebrate a festival for the Lord your God in the place that the Lord your God will choose for himself. When the Lord your God blesses you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, you will rejoice.

Three times a year every male shall stand before the Lord your God in the place that the Lord your God will choose for you: at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, at the Festival of Weeks, and at the Festival of Tabernacles. You must not stand before the Lord your God empty-handed.
Each person shall give according to what he can afford, according to the blessing that the Lord your God has given you.

You shall appoint your judges and those who guide you in instruction over you in all your towns that the Lord your God will give you, according to your tribes. They shall judge the people with just judgment.
They must not distort justice, show partiality, or accept bribes, for bribes blind the eyes of the wise and take away truthful words.

You shall take care to administer justice truthfully, so that you may live and enter and take possession of the land that the Lord your God will give you, tribe by tribe. And they shall judge the people with just judgment.
You must not plant for yourself a grove of any kind of tree beside the altar of the Lord your God. You must not make for yourself [?] on these.
You must not set up for yourself a pillar of the kind that the Lord your God hates.
You must not slaughter for the Lord your God an ox or a sheep that has a defect. Every evil thing is an abomination to the Lord your God.
If a man or woman is found in one of your towns that the Lord your God will give you, doing evil before the Lord your God by abandoning his covenant,
and they go and serve other gods and worship them, or the sun or the moon or any of those belonging to the array of heaven, which I did not command,
When you are told, investigate it very carefully. If you find that the report is indeed true, that this abomination has happened in Israel,
You shall bring out that man or that woman, and they shall stone them to death.
On the testimony of two witnesses or three witnesses, the person who is to be put to death shall die. He must not die on the testimony of only one witness.

The witnesses shall be the first to raise their hands against him to kill him, and afterward all the people shall raise their hands against him. You shall remove the wicked person from—from among you.

If a case is too difficult for you, beyond your ability to decide, between one case of bloodshed and another, between one judgment and another, between one injustice and another, or between one sore and another—cases of judgment in your towns—you shall get up and go to the place that the Lord your God will choose for himself, so that his name may be invoked there.
You shall go to the Levites or to the judge who is serving in those days. They shall investigate and tell you the judgment.

You shall act according to the instruction they give you in the place that the Lord your God has chosen for his name to be proclaimed there. You shall take great care to do everything according to the provision of the law that they establish for you.
You shall act according to the judgment they tell you. You must not turn aside from what they tell you, either to the right or to the left.

But anyone who acts arrogantly, refusing to obey the priest who stands ministering in the name of the Lord your God, or the judge serving in those days, and does not listen to them—that person must die. You must remove the evil person from Israel.
When all the people hear, they will be afraid and will not act presumptuously again.

When you enter the land that the Lord your God will give you as an inheritance, take possession of it, and settle in it, and you say, “I will appoint a ruler over myself like the other nations around me,”

you shall certainly appoint over yourself a ruler whom the Lord your God will choose. You shall appoint the ruler over yourself from among your own people. You must not appoint a foreigner over yourself, because he is not one of your own people.
For he must not acquire many horses for himself or send the people back to Egypt to acquire many horses for himself. The Lord has said, “You must not go back that way again.”
He must not take many wives for himself, nor must his heart turn away. He must not accumulate excessive amounts of silver and gold for himself.
And when he takes his seat as ruler, he must write for himself a copy of this law in a book, from the copy held by the Levitical priests.
It shall remain with him, and he shall read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the Lord your God and keep all these commandments and statutes by carrying them out.

So that his heart will not become proud toward his brothers, and he will not turn aside from the commandments to the right or to the left, so that he and his children with him may reign for a long time among the people of Israel.
The Levitical priests are to have no share or inheritance with Israel. The sacrifices of the Lord are their inheritance; these are what they will eat.
He must have no inheritance among his brothers. The Lord himself is his inheritance, just as he told him.

And this is the priests’ rightful due, which they will receive from the people, from those who slaughter animals for sacrifice: whether it is an ox or a sheep, the person must give the priest the shoulder, the cheeks, and the stomach.
And you must give him the first portion of your grain, your wine, and your oil, and the first portion of the wool shorn from your sheep.

For the Lord your God has chosen him out of all your tribes to stand before the Lord your God, to minister and to bless in his name, together with his other sons among the people of Israel, all their days.
But if a Levite comes to you from any of your towns among all the people of Israel, from the place where he is staying, as he himself desires, to the place that the Lord your God will choose,
he is to serve in the name of the Lord his God, like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the Lord.
He is to eat an allotted share, apart from what is set aside for him through his family inheritance.
When you enter the land that the Lord your God will give you, you must not learn to practice the detestable acts of those nations.
No one who [?] shall be found among you, purifying his son or daughter in fire, practicing divination, interpreting omens, observing signs, practicing sorcery, or casting spells.
Or a ventriloquist, or someone who pays attention to signs and consults the dead.
For everyone who does this is detestable to the Lord your God. Because of these detestable acts, the Lord will drive them out before you.
You must be holy before the Lord your God.
For these nations whose land you will inherit listen to people who cast lots and practice divination. But the Lord your God has not permitted you to do this.
The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers, and you must listen to him.

In accordance with everything you asked of the Lord your God at Horeb in the days of the assembly, when you said, “We must not continue to hear the voice of the Lord our God, and we must not continue to see this great fire, so that we do not die.”
And the Lord said to me, “Everything they have said is right.
I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their brothers, and I will speak into his mouth. He will speak to them according to what I command him.
And I myself will punish the person who does not listen to the words that the prophet will speak in my name.
But if a prophet acts wickedly by speaking a word in my name that I did not command him to speak, or speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet must die.
If you say in your heart, “How will we recognize a word that the Lord has not spoken?”
If that prophet speaks in my name and the word does not happen or come true, this is a word that the Lord has not spoken. The prophet has spoken it presumptuously. You must not let him go.
When the Lord your God destroys the nations whose land your God will give you, and you take possession of them and live in their towns and their houses,
you must set apart three towns for yourself in the midst of the land that the Lord your God will give you.

Prepare the road for yourself, and divide the territory of your land into three parts—the land that the Lord your God will allot to you—so that they may be places of refuge for anyone who kills someone.
The person who flees there will live: someone who kills his neighbor unintentionally and who had not previously hated him.

If someone goes into a wooded place with his neighbor to cut wood, and his hand slips while he is cutting the wood with an axe, and the iron head comes off the handle and strikes his neighbor so that he dies, that person shall flee to one of these cities and live.

This is so that the avenger of the dead man will not pursue the killer because his heart is burning with anger against him, overtake him if the journey is long, and strike him dead. Yet this person [?] must not be considered deserving of death, because he had not previously hated the other man.
Therefore I give you this command: Set apart three cities for yourself.
If the Lord your God enlarges your territory, as the Lord your God swore to your ancestors, and the Lord gives you all the land that the Lord promised to give your ancestors,

provided you obey and carry out all these commandments that I am giving you today, loving the Lord your God and walking in all his ways throughout your life, you shall add three more cities to these three cities.
