Then innocent blood will not be shed in your land, which the Lord your God will give you as an inheritance, and no one among you will be held accountable for having shed blood.
But if someone hates his neighbor, lies in wait for him, rises up against him, strikes him dead, and flees into one of these cities,
the elders of his city shall send for him, take him from that place, and hand him over to the dead man's relative, who shall kill him.
You must not pity him. You shall remove the stain of innocent blood from Israel, so that things may go well for you.
You must not move your neighbor's boundary markers, which those before you established in the inheritance given to you in the land that the Lord your God will give you as an inheritance.

A single witness shall not be sufficient to testify against someone concerning any wrongdoing or any sin he commits. Rather, every matter shall be established by the testimony of two witnesses and by the testimony of three witnesses.
If an unjust witness comes forward against someone, accusing him of wrongdoing,
the two people who are disputing with each other shall stand before the Lord, before the priests, and before the judges who are serving in those days.
The judges shall investigate thoroughly. If it turns out that the witness is unjust and has given false testimony against his brother,
you shall remove the evil person from among you.
When the others hear, they will be afraid and will no longer do such a thing among you.
You must not pity him: give life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

When you go out to war to fight your enemies and see a horse and its rider, and a multitude greater than you, do not be afraid of them, because the Lord your God is with you, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
When you approach the battle, the priest shall come forward to the people.

He will speak with them and say to them, “Listen, Israel! Today you are going out against your enemies to fight them. Do not let your hearts be troubled or become faint. Do not fear them, do not be alarmed, and do not collapse before them.”
For the Lord your God is the one who goes ahead of you. He will help you fight your enemies and save you.

The officials shall speak to the people, saying, “Who has built a new house but has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, so that he does not die in battle and another man dedicate it.”
“And who has planted a vineyard but has not enjoyed its produce? Let him go and return to his house, so that he does not die in battle and another man enjoy its produce.”
And who is the man who has become engaged to a woman but has not yet married her? Let him go and return to his house, so that he does not die in the war and another man marry her.

The scribes shall continue speaking to the people, saying, “Who is the man who is afraid and fainthearted? Let him go and return to his house, so that he does not die and does not make his brother’s heart weak like his own.”
When the scribes have finished speaking before the people, they shall appoint leaders over the multitude to lead the people.
When you approach a city to fight against it, call on its people to make peace.
If they answer you with peaceful words and open up to you, all the people found in that city shall pay tribute to you and obey you.
But if they do not submit to you and instead stand up to fight against you, you shall besiege it.
The Lord your God shall deliver it into your hands, and you shall kill every male in it with the sword.

But their women, their children, all their livestock, everything in the city, and all their supplies you shall take for yourself. You shall consume all the plunder of your enemies that the Lord your God will deliver into your hands.
This is what you shall do to all the cities that are far from you and are not among the cities of these nations.
But look: in the cities of these nations that the Lord your God will deliver into your hands so that you may inherit their land, you shall not keep anyone alive.
Instead, you shall utterly destroy them: the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites, just as the Lord your God commanded you.
This is so that they do not teach you to practice the detestable things they did for their gods, causing you to sin before the Lord your God.

When you besiege a city for many days, fighting against it to capture it, you shall not destroy its trees by bringing an axe against them to cut them down. Instead, you shall eat from them, but you shall not cut down the trees. Is a tree in the field a human being, to come before you into the siege?

But a tree whose fruit you know is not edible is one you may cut down and destroy. You shall build siegeworks against the city that you are standing against in battle, until it is delivered into your hands.
If someone is found murdered in the land that the Lord your God will give you to inherit, lying in the field, and no one knows who killed him,
your elders and your judges shall go out and measure the distance to the city nearest the murdered person.
The elders of that city shall bring a heifer down into a valley—a heifer that has never been used for work and has never borne a yoke.
The elders of that city shall take it down into a rugged valley that has never been worked or plowed, and they shall break the heifer’s neck there.

The Levitical priests shall come forward, because they are the ones the Lord your God chose to stand before him to serve and to bless in his name. The judgment of every dispute and every matter shall rest on their word.
All the elders of that city nearest the murdered person shall wash their hands over the head of the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley.
They shall answer, saying, “Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see it.
“Lord, forgive your people Israel, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, so that innocent blood will not be charged against your people Israel.” And he will forgive them for the bloodshed.
You shall remove the innocent blood from your midst, and good shall come to you if you do what is pleasing and good before the Lord your God.
When you go out to war against your enemies, and the Lord your God delivers them into your hands, and you take their captives,
And if you see among the captives a woman who is beautiful, and you desire her and take her as your wife,
you shall bring her into your house, shave her head, and trim her nails.

You shall have her take off the clothes she wore as a captive. She shall stay in your house, mourning her father and mother for a full month. After this, you may go in to her and have relations with her, and she shall become your wife.
And if you do not want her, you must send her away free. You must not sell her for money, and you must not mistreat her, because you have humiliated her.
If one man has two wives, one whom he loves and another whom he hates, and both the loved wife and the hated wife bear him children, and the firstborn son belongs to the hated wife,
And on the day when he gives his possessions to his sons as an inheritance, he must not make the son of the loved woman the firstborn, overlooking the son of the hated woman, who is the firstborn.
he shall instead acknowledge the hated wife's firstborn, giving him a double share of everything he owns, because this son is the first of his children, and the rights of the firstborn belong to him.
But if someone has a disobedient son who defies him and does not listen to his father and mother, and who still does not listen to them when they discipline him, his father and mother must seize him.
They shall bring him before the elders of their city, at the gate of their gathering place.

They shall say to the people of their city, 'This son of ours does not obey us but provokes us, and he does not listen to what we say. He takes part in drinking parties, drinks wine, and is a drunkard.'
The people of their city shall stone him with stones until he dies. You shall remove the evil from among you, and the others will hear and be afraid.
If someone is guilty of an offense deserving a death sentence, and you hang him on a tree,

his body must not remain on the tree. Instead, you must bury him that same day, because everyone hung on a tree is cursed by God. You must not defile the land that the Lord your God will give you as an inheritance.
Do not see your brother's ox or sheep straying on the road and ignore them. Instead, you must bring them back to your brother and give them to him.

If your brother does not live near you and you do not know him, you shall bring them into your house. They shall remain with you until your brother searches for them, and then you shall give them to him.

You shall do the same with his donkey, and with his ox or his clothing. You shall do the same with anything your brother has lost—anything he may lose and you find. You must not walk away and leave it.
You must not see your brother's donkey or ox fallen on the road and ignore them. Instead, you shall help him and raise them up.
A woman must not wear a man's equipment, nor must a man put on a woman's clothing, because everyone who does these things is detestable to the Lord your God.

If you come upon a bird's nest along your way, in any tree or on the ground, with chicks or eggs in it, and the mother is sitting on her chicks or on the eggs, you must not take the mother along with the young.
Instead, you must let the mother go, but you may take her young for yourself, so that things may go well for you and you may live many days.
If you build a new house, you shall build a protective wall around its roof, so that no death occurs at your house if someone falls from it.
You must not sow your vineyard with two kinds of seed, lest the produce become defiled, both the seed you sow and the produce of your plot—your vineyard.
You must not plow with an ox or a donkey together under one yoke.
You must not wear clothing made from a mixture of wool and linen woven together.
You shall put tassels on the four corners of the garments you wear.
If a man takes a wife, has relations with her, and then hates her,
and brings accusations against her and gives her a bad reputation, saying, 'I took this woman to live with her, but when I approached her, I found no evidence of her virginity,'
the young woman's father and mother shall take the evidence of the young woman's virginity and display it before the elders at the gathering place.
And the young woman's father shall say before the elders, “I gave this daughter of mine to this man as his wife, and when he came to hate her,

now he accuses her with slanderous words, saying, ‘I found no evidence of your daughter's virginity in her.’ Here, then, is the evidence of my daughter's virginity.” And they shall spread out the cloth before the elders of the city.
And the elders of that city shall take that man and discipline him.

They must impose a fine of a hundred shekels on him and give them to the young woman’s father, because he has spread a bad name about a virgin of Israel. She must remain his wife, and he may not divorce her for the rest of his life.
But if this accusation is true, and no evidence of the young woman's virginity is found,

They must bring the young woman out to the door of her father’s house, and the men of her town must stone her to death, because she has done a disgraceful thing among the people of Israel by committing sexual immorality in her father’s house. You must remove the evil person from among you.

If they find a man sleeping with a woman who lives with her husband, you shall put them both to death—the man sleeping with the woman, and the woman as well. And you shall remove the evil from among you.
If there is a young virgin who is engaged to a husband, and a man finds her in the city and sleeps with her,

you shall bring both of them out to the city gate, and they shall stone them to death: the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he violated his neighbor's wife. And you shall remove the evil from among you.
But if a man finds the engaged young woman in the countryside and takes her by force and sleeps with her, you shall put to death only the man who slept with her,
you must do nothing to the young woman. She has committed no sin deserving death, because this case is like that of a man who attacks his neighbor and kills him.
because he found her in the countryside, and the engaged young woman cried out, but she found no one to help her.
If someone finds a young virgin who is not engaged, and takes her by force and sleeps with her, and they catch him,
the man who slept with her shall give the young woman's father fifty silver staters, and she shall become his wife because he violated her. He shall not be able to divorce her for his whole life.
A man shall not take his neighbor's wife or his father's wife, and he shall not uncover his father's bed.
A man whose genitals are crushed or cut off must not enter the assembly of the Lord.
Someone born of a prostitute shall not enter the assembly of the Lord.
An Ammonite or a Moabite shall not enter the assembly of the Lord, even to the twelfth generation and forever,
because they did not come out to meet you with bread and water on the road when you were coming out of Egypt, and because they hired Balaam son of Beor, from Mesopotamia in Syria, to curse you.
But the Lord your God was not willing to listen to Balaam, and the Lord your God turned the curses into blessings, because the Lord your God loved you.
You must never speak to them of peace or of what benefits them, for all time.
You shall not detest an Edomite, because he is your brother. You shall not detest an Egyptian, because you lived as a foreigner in his land.
Children born to them in the third generation shall enter the assembly of the Lord.
When you go out against your enemies to fight them, you shall keep yourself from every evil thing.
If there is a man with you who is not clean because of his nighttime emission, he shall stay outside the camp and shall not enter it.
In the evening he shall wash his body with water, and when the sun sets he shall enter the camp.
You shall have a place outside the camp, and you shall go out to that place.
You shall have a digging tool on the belt fastened around you. When you squat outside, you shall dig with it, turn the earth over, and cover your excrement with it.

For the Lord your God will walk about in your camp to protect you and to deliver your enemy into your hands. Your camp shall be holy, so that nothing indecent is found among you and he does not turn away from you.
You must not hand a slave over to his master if his master has [?] him to you.
He shall live with you and stay among you in whatever place pleases him. You must not oppress him.

There must be no prostitute among the daughters of Israel and no male prostitute among the sons of Israel. There must be no woman among the daughters of Israel who performs or receives initiation rites, and no man among the sons of Israel who performs initiation rites.
You must not bring a prostitute's earnings or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord your God in fulfillment of any vow, because these are detestable to the Lord your God.
You must not charge your brother interest on money or food, or interest on anything that you lend your brother at interest.
You may charge a foreigner interest, but you must not charge your brother interest, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all your work in the land that you are entering to possess.
If you make a vow to the Lord your God, you must not delay fulfilling it, because the Lord your God will thoroughly examine all your deeds. Otherwise, you will be guilty of sin.
But if you do not wish to make a vow, you will not be guilty of sin.
Be careful to carry out what comes from your lips, just as you vowed to the Lord your God—the words you spoke with your mouth.
If you enter your neighbor’s field, you may pluck ears of grain with your hands and eat them, but you must not take a sickle to your neighbor’s field.
If you enter your neighbor’s vineyard, you may eat as many grapes as you wish until you are satisfied, but you must not gather any into a container of your own.

If a man takes a wife and lives with her, and she does not find favor in his eyes because he has found something shameful about her, he shall write her a certificate of divorce, put it in her hand, and send her out of his house.
And if she goes and lives with another husband,
and the second husband hates her and writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand, and sends her out of his house, or the second husband who took her as his wife dies,

the first husband, who sent her away, cannot return to her and take her as his wife after she has been defiled, because this is detestable in the sight of the Lord your God. You must not defile the land that the Lord your God will give you as an inheritance.

If a man takes a new wife, he must not go out to fight in war, and no duty must be imposed on him. He shall spend a year at home without any duty being imposed on him, rejoicing with the wife he has taken.
You must not take a millstone as collateral, nor the stone used for grinding on it, because doing this takes a person’s life as collateral.
If a man is caught kidnapping someone from among his brothers, the people of Israel, and overpowering him and selling him, that kidnapper must die. You must remove the evil person from among you.
Be on your guard concerning leprosy. Be very careful to act according to the whole law that the Levitical priests will declare to you, just as I commanded you to do.
Remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam on the road when you were coming out of Egypt.
If your neighbor owes you money or anything else, you must not enter his house to take his collateral.
Instead, you shall stand outside, and the man who owes you shall bring his collateral out to you.
If the man is poor, you must not keep his collateral inside your house.

You must return his garment to him when the sun is setting, so that his garment may cover him and he may bless you. This will be counted as an act of mercy on your part in the sight of the Lord your God.
You must not act unjustly concerning the [?] of a poor laborer, whether he is one of your brothers or one of the resident foreigners in your towns.

You shall give him his wages immediately, before the sun sets, because he is poor and his life depends on them. Otherwise, he may cry out to the Lord against you, and it will be counted against you as a sin.
Parents must not die for their children, and children must not die for their parents. Each person shall die for his own sin.
You must not deny justice to the resident foreigner, the orphan, or the widow, and you must not take a widow’s garment as a pledge.
Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt and that the Lord your God redeemed you from there. That is why I command you to do this.

When you reap your harvest in the field and forget a sheaf in the field, you must not go back to get it. Instead, leave it behind for the poor, the resident foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all your work.

When you come to gather the olives from your olive grove, you must not go back to gather what remains. Instead, leave it for the resident foreigner, the orphan, and the widow. Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt. That is why I command you to do this.
When you harvest your vineyard, you must not go back to glean it. Instead, what remains shall belong to the resident foreigner, the orphan, and the widow.
Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt. That is why I command you to do this.
But if a dispute arises between people and they come for judgment, they must be judged: the wicked person must be condemned, and the righteous person acquitted.
If the guilty person deserves a beating, you shall make him sit down before the judges, and they shall flog him in their presence according to his wrongdoing.
They shall give him forty lashes and no more. If they go on flogging him beyond these lashes, your brother will be disgraced in your sight.
You must not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.

If brothers live together and one of them dies without leaving offspring, his wife must not marry another man, a stranger outside the family. Her husband’s brother shall go in to her, take her as his wife, and live with her.
The little boy who is born must be named after the man who died, so that his name will not disappear from Israel.

But if the man is unwilling to marry his brother’s wife, the woman must go to the assembly of the elders and say, “Her husband’s brother is unwilling to preserve his brother’s name in Israel. Her husband’s brother has refused to do this.”
The elders of that city shall summon him and speak to him. If he stands firm and says, “I do not want to marry her,”

his brother’s wife shall approach him in the presence of the elders, undo the strap of the sandal on his foot, spit in his face, and say, “This is what shall be done to the man who will not build up his brother’s household.”
And in Israel his name will be called “The household of the man whose sandal was removed.”

If two men are fighting with each other, a man and his brother, and the wife of one of them approaches to rescue her husband from the man striking him, and she reaches out her hand and grabs his genitals,
you shall cut off her hand. You must show her no pity.
You must not have both a large weight and a small weight in your bag.
You must not have differing measures in your house, a large one and a small one.
You shall have a true and just weight, and you shall have a true and just measure, so that you may live many days in the land that the Lord your God will give you as an inheritance.
Everyone who does these things, everyone who acts unjustly, is detestable to the Lord your God.
Remember what Amalek did to you on the road when you were coming out of Egypt,
how he attacked you on the road and destroyed the weary people at your rear. You were hungry and weary, and besides all this, you did not fear God.

When the Lord your God gives you rest from all your enemies around you in the land that the Lord your God will give you as an inheritance to possess, you shall erase the name of Amalek from under heaven.
And you must not forget. When you enter the land that the Lord your God will give you as an inheritance to possess, and you settle in it,

You must take some of the firstfruits of the crops you bring in from your land, which the Lord your God will give you as an inheritance. Put them in a basket and go to the place the Lord your God will choose for himself, so that his name may be invoked there.
Go to the priest who is serving in those days and say to him, “I declare to the Lord my God that I have entered the land that the Lord swore to our ancestors to give us.”
The priest must take the basket from your hand and set it down before the altar of the Lord your God.

Then you must answer and say before the Lord your God, “My father left Syria behind and went down to Egypt. He lived there as a foreigner with a small number of people, and there he became a great nation, a large and numerous multitude.
The Egyptians oppressed us, humiliated us, and imposed hard labor on us.
We cried out to the Lord, the God of our ancestors, and the Lord heard our voice. He saw our humiliation, our hardship, and our distress.
The Lord brought us out of Egypt with great power, a strong hand, and an uplifted arm, with great visions, signs, and wonders.
He brought us into this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.

And now, look, I have brought the firstfruits of the produce of the land that you, Lord, gave me, a land flowing with milk and honey.” You must set it before the Lord your God and worship there before the Lord your God.
You must rejoice in all the good things that the Lord your God has given you, together with your household, the Levite, and the foreigner living with you.

When you have finished giving the entire tithe of your land's produce in the third year, you must give the second tithe to the Levite, the foreign resident, the orphan, and the widow, so that they may eat in your towns and be satisfied.

You must say before the Lord your God, “I have removed my vowed offerings from my house and given them to the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, according to all the commandments you gave me. I have neither transgressed your commandment nor forgotten it.

I have not eaten any of them while mourning, nor left any of them behind as something spoiled and unclean. I have not given any of them to someone who has died. I have obeyed the voice of the Lord my God and done as he commanded me.”
Look down from your holy dwelling, from heaven, and bless your people Israel and the land you have given them, just as you swore to our ancestors to give us a land flowing with milk and honey.
Today the Lord your God has commanded you to carry out all these ordinances and judgments. You must observe them and carry them out with all your heart and all your soul.
God has chosen you today so that he may be your God, if you walk in his ways, keep his commandments, his ordinances, and his judgments, and obey his voice.
The Lord has chosen you today to be his honored people, as he said, so that you may keep all his commandments,
and so that you may be exalted above all the nations, as he has established you, renowned, praised, and glorified, and so that you may be a people holy to the Lord your God, as he said.
Moses and the elders of Israel gave this command: “Keep all these commandments that I am commanding you today.”
And on the day when you cross the Jordan into the land that the Lord your God will give you, you must set up these two large stones and coat them with plaster.
Write on the stones all the words of this law when you cross the Jordan to enter the land flowing with milk and honey, just as the Lord, the God of your ancestors, told you.
When you cross the Jordan, you must set up these stones, about which I am giving you instructions, on Mount Ebal, and coat them with plaster.
There you must build an altar of stones to the Lord your God, using whole stones. You must not apply an iron tool to them.
You must offer burnt offerings on them to the Lord your God.
And offer a sacrifice of well-being there to the Lord your God. Eat there and be satisfied, and rejoice before the Lord your God.
You must write this entire law on these stones, writing it very clearly.”
Moses, together with the priests and the Levites, spoke before Israel: “Today you have become the people of the Lord your God.”
You must obey the voice of the Lord your God and carry out all his commandments and his ordinances that I am giving you.”
On that day Moses gave instructions to the people, saying:
These are the ones who will stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people when you cross the Jordan: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
And these are the ones who will stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
And the Levites will respond and say to all the men of Israel in a loud voice:

“Cursed is the person who makes himself a carved image or a cast image, for it is detestable to the Lord, a work made by the hands of craftsmen of this kind, and puts it in a hidden place.” And the people will respond and say, “So be it.”
“Cursed is anyone who dishonors his father or his mother.” And all the people will say, “So be it.”
“Cursed is anyone who moves his neighbor’s boundary markers.” And all the people will say, “So be it.”
“Cursed is anyone who leads a blind person astray from the road.” And all the people will say, “So be it.”
“Cursed is anyone who perverts justice for the foreign resident, the orphan, or the widow.” And all the people will say, “So be it.”
“Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his father’s wife, because he has uncovered his father’s bed.” And all the people will say, “So be it.”
“Cursed is anyone who sleeps with any animal.” And all the people will say, “So be it.”
“Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his sister, whether she shares his father or his mother.” And all the people will say, “So be it.”
Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his father's sister. And all the people shall say, “So be it.”
“Cursed is anyone who strikes his neighbor through deceit.” And all the people will say, “So be it.”
Cursed is anyone who accepts a bribe to kill someone and shed innocent blood. And all the people shall say, “So be it.”
“Cursed is anyone who does not uphold the words of this law by carrying them out.” And all the people will say, “So be it.”

And when you cross the Jordan into the land that the Lord your God will give you, if you obey the voice of the Lord your God, carefully carrying out all his commandments that I give you today, the Lord your God will set you above all the nations of the earth.
And all these blessings will come upon you and bless you if you obey the voice of the Lord your God.
You will be blessed in the city and blessed in your field.
And your children will be blessed, as will the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep.
And your storehouses will be blessed, along with the things you have stored in them.
And you will be blessed when you go in and when you come out.
The Lord your God will deliver into your hands your enemies who have fought against you, defeated before you. They will come out against you by one road, but they will flee before you by seven roads.
The Lord your God will send blessing into your storehouse and upon all the work you undertake in the land that the Lord your God will give you.
The Lord will establish you as a holy people, just as the Lord swore to your ancestors, if you obey the voice of the Lord your God and walk in his ways.
All the nations of the earth will see that the name of the Lord your God has been proclaimed over you, and they will fear him.

And the Lord your God has made you abound in good things—in your children, the produce of your land, and the offspring of your livestock—on the land that the Lord swore to your ancestors he would give you.

The Lord will open for you his treasury of good things, which is heaven, [?] to give it at the proper time, for he will bless all the work of your hands. You will lend at interest to many nations, but you yourself will not borrow at interest.

And you will rule over many nations, but they will not rule over you. The Lord your God will make you the head and not the tail. You will be above them and not below, if you obey the commandments of the Lord your God, which I command you today to keep and carry out.
You must not turn aside, to the right or to the left, from the words that I command you today, going after other, foreign gods to serve them.
But if you do not obey the voice of the Lord your God by keeping and carrying out all his commandments, which I command you today, these curses will come upon you and overtake you.
You will be cursed in the city, and you will be cursed in the countryside.
Your storehouses and the things you have in them will be cursed.
Your offspring will be cursed, along with the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep.
You will be cursed when you come in, and you will be cursed when you go out.

The Lord your God will send deprivation, hunger, and destruction upon you, upon every task you undertake [?], among the things you do, until he wipes you out and destroys you immediately because of your evil deeds, because you have abandoned me.
The Lord will send death against you until he wipes you out from the land you are entering to inherit.
The Lord will bring upon you wasting disease, fever, chills, inflammation, slaughter, blight, and mildew. These will come upon you until they wipe you out.
The sky above you will become bronze over you, and the ground beneath you will become like iron.
The Lord will make the rain of your land dry earth falling upon you from the sky, until he destroys you and wipes you out.

The Lord will set your enemies after you. You will go out against them by one road, but you will scatter before them, fleeing by seven roads. You will be scattered throughout all the kingdoms of the earth.
Your dead will become food for the birds of the sky and the wild animals of the earth, and no one will drive them away from them.
The Lord will afflict you with the boils of Egypt, severe scabies, and itching, so that you will be unable to find relief from them.
The Lord will bring upon you great madness and blindness, with confusion of mind.

You will grope at midday as a blind person gropes in the darkness, and he will not make your paths straight. At that time you will be oppressed and robbed every day, and there will be no one to help you.
You will take a wife, but someone else will take her away from you. You will build a house, but you will not live in it. You will plant a vineyard, but you will not harvest its grapes.

Your ox will be slaughtered before your eyes, but you will not eat any of it. Your donkey will be seized from you and will not be returned to you. Your sheep will be handed over to your enemies, and you will find no one to help you.
Your sons and daughters will be handed over to another nation, and your eyes will not see them. Your eyes will grow weary looking for them, and your hand will be powerless to do anything.
Another nation, one unknown to you, will eat the produce of your fields and everything you have worked for. You will be oppressed and crushed all your days.
You will go mad because of the things your eyes see happening before you.
The Lord will bring painful boils upon your knees and your legs, from the soles of your feet to the crown of your head, and you will be unable to recover.
The Lord will take you and the other rulers you appoint over yourself to a nation that neither you nor your ancestors have known. There you will serve other gods made of wood and stone.
There you will become a spectacle, a proverb, and a saying among all the nations into which the Lord will take you.
You will sow much seed in your field, but you will gather little, because the locusts will eat it.
You will plant a vineyard and work in it, but you will not drink its wine or enjoy it, because worms will eat the grapes.
You will have olive trees throughout your territory, but you will not anoint yourself with their oil, because your olive trees will shed their fruit on the ground.
You will father sons and daughters, but they will not be left with you, for they will be taken into captivity.
Blight will destroy all your trees and all the produce of your land.
The foreigner who lives among you will rise higher and higher above you, while you will sink lower and lower beneath him.
He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head over you, but you will be like a tail.

All these curses will come upon you and pursue you until they destroy you, because you did not obey the voice of the Lord your God and keep his commandments and ordinances, which he commanded you to observe.
And they will be signs and wonders among you and among your descendants forever.
Because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and a glad heart because of the abundance of all you had produced,
There you will serve your enemies, whom the Lord will bring against you, in hunger, thirst, nakedness, and a lack of everything. He will put an iron yoke on your neck until he destroys you.
The Lord will bring against you a nation from far away, from the end of the earth, whose flight is like an eagle’s flight—a nation whose language you will not be able to understand.
A fierce-faced nation that will show no respect for an old person and no mercy to a young child.
It will eat the offspring of your livestock and the crops of your land, leaving you no grain, wine, or oil, nor the offspring of your cattle or the young of your sheep, until it destroys you.

It will besiege you in your cities until your high, fortified cities, in which you trust, are brought down throughout your land. It will oppress you in all your cities that the Lord your God has given you.

you will eat the flesh of the offspring of your womb [?], your sons and daughters whom the Lord gave you. You will eat them during your siege and in the distress with which the enemy will oppress you.
The man who is tender and very delicate will be spiteful toward his brother, his beloved wife, and the children who are left among the survivors,

over giving any of them some of the flesh of his children whom he will eat, because nothing has been left for him in the siege and distress with which your enemies will oppress you in all your cities.

The tender and delicate woman among you, who has never ventured to put her feet on the ground because of her delicate refinement, will be spiteful toward her beloved husband, her son, and her daughter,

and toward her afterbirth that came out from between her thighs and the child she will bear. She will immediately eat it in secret because of the lack of everything, in the siege and distress with which your enemy will oppress you in your cities.
If you do not obey and carry out all the words of this law written in this book, so that you fear this great, honored, wonderful name—the Lord your God—
the Lord will multiply your afflictions and the afflictions of your descendants: great, severe afflictions and severe, lasting diseases.
And he will bring back upon you all the terrible suffering of Egypt that you feared, and these troubles will come upon you.
The Lord will also bring upon you every sickness and every plague not written in the book of this law, until he destroys you.
You will be left few in number, although you were as numerous as the stars of heaven, because you did not obey the voice of the Lord your God.
Just as the Lord delighted in doing every good thing for you and multiplying you, so the Lord will delight in destroying you. You will be uprooted from the land you are entering to possess.
The Lord your God will scatter you among all the nations, from one end of the earth to the other. There you will serve other gods of wood and stone, which neither you nor your ancestors have known.
He will give you no rest among those other nations, and your feet will find no resting place there. The Lord will give you there an anxious heart, failing eyes, and an exhausted soul.
Your life will hang before your eyes. You will be afraid by day and by night, and you will have no confidence in your life.

In the morning you will say, “When will evening come?” And in the evening you will say, “When will morning come?” This will be because of the fear in your heart at the things you will fear, and because of the sights your eyes will see.

And the Lord will take you back to Egypt in ships, by the route about which I said, “You will never see it again.” And there I will sell you to your enemies as male and female slaves, but no one will buy you.
These are the words of the covenant that the Lord commanded Moses to establish with the people of Israel in the land of Moab, after the covenant that he made with them at Horeb.
And Moses called all the children of Israel and said to them, “You have seen the deeds that the Lord did in the land of Egypt before Pharaoh, his servants, and all his land.
the great trials your eyes saw, the signs, and those great wonders.
Yet to this day the Lord God has not given you a heart to know him, eyes to see, or ears to hear.
He led you for forty years in the wilderness. Your clothes did not wear out, and your sandals did not wear out on your feet.
You ate no bread and drank no wine or strong drink, so that you would understand that the Lord is your God.
You reached this place, and Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to fight against us, and we defeated them.
We took their land, and I gave it as an inheritance to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh.
You must be careful to carry out all the words of this covenant, so that you may understand all the things you will do.
All of you are standing today before the Lord your God: the rulers of your tribes, your elders, your judges, your scribes and teachers, and everyone in Israel.
your wives, your children, and the foreigner living within your camp, from your woodcutter to your water carrier,
so that you may enter into the covenant of the Lord your God and into his oaths, which the Lord your God will establish with you today,
so that he may establish you as his people and become your God, just as he told you and as he swore to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
I am not establishing this covenant and these oaths with you alone.
But also with the others who are here with you today before the Lord your God, and with the others who are not here with you today.
For you know how we lived in the land of Egypt and how we passed through the nations through which you passed.
You saw their abominations and their idols of wood and stone, silver and gold, which they possess.

Is there among you a man or woman, a family or tribe, whose heart has turned away from the Lord your God to go and worship the gods of the nations? Is there anyone among you who is a root sprouting up with gall and bitterness?
If he hears the words of this curse and boasts, saying in his heart, “May I remain pure, for I will follow the desire of my heart,” lest the sinner destroy the innocent along with himself,

God will not be willing to forgive him. Instead, on that day the Lord’s anger and jealousy will blaze against that person, and all the curses of this covenant written in the book of this law will come down upon him. And the Lord will erase his name from under heaven.
And the Lord will set [?] apart for disaster from among all the children of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant written in the book of this law.
The generation of your children who arise after you, and the foreigner who comes from a distant land, will speak when they see the plagues of that land and the diseases the Lord has sent upon it:

sulfur and salt, with that whole land burning. It will not be sown, nor will any vegetation sprout in it, just as Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim were destroyed—the places the Lord destroyed in anger and wrath.
All the nations of the earth will say, “Why has the Lord done these things to this land? What is the reason for this great anger and this wrath?”
And they will say, “Because they abandoned the covenant of the Lord their God, the God of their ancestors, which he made with them when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.
And they went and served other gods and worshiped them—gods they did not know and that he had not assigned to them.
And the Lord became fiercely angry with that land, bringing upon it all the curses written in the book of this law.
And the Lord uprooted them from their land in anger, wrath, and very great fury, and threw them into another land, where they are now.”
The hidden things belong to the Lord our God, but the revealed things belong to you and your children forever, so that you may carry out all the words of this law.
And when all these words come upon you—the blessing and the curse that I have set before you—you will take them to heart among all the nations where the Lord will scatter you.
And you will return to the Lord your God and obey his voice according to every word that I command you today, with all your heart and all your soul.
And the Lord will forgive your sins and have mercy on you, and he will gather you again from all the nations where the Lord scattered you.
And even if you have been scattered from one end of heaven to the other, the Lord your God will gather you from there.
And the Lord your God will bring you into the land that your ancestors inherited, and you will inherit it. He will do good to you and make you more numerous than your ancestors.
And he will cleanse your heart and the heart of your descendants, so that you may love the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul, and so that you and your descendants may live.
And the Lord your God will put these curses upon your enemies and upon those who hate you, who persecuted you.
And you will return and obey the voice of the Lord your God and carry out his commandments, which I command you today.

And the Lord your God will take great care of you in all the work of your hands, in your offspring, in the produce of your land, and in the young of your livestock. For the Lord your God will again rejoice over you by doing good to you, just as he rejoiced over your ancestors.

If you obey the voice of the Lord your God, keeping and carrying out his commandments and his statutes written in the book of this law, if you return to the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul.
For this commandment that I command you [?] is not too difficult for you, nor is it far from you.
So that you would say, “Who among us will go up to heaven and bring it to us, so that we may hear it and do it?”
Nor is it on the other side of the sea, so that you would say, “Who among us will cross to the other side of the sea and bring it to us and let us hear it, so that we may do it?”
But the word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart and in your hand, so that you may do it.
Look, today I have set before you life and death, good and evil.

But if you obey the commandments of the Lord your God, which I command you today—to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, and to keep his statutes and his judgments—you will live and increase, and the Lord your God will bless you throughout the land that you are entering to inherit.
But if your heart turns away and you do not listen, but go astray and worship other gods and serve them,
I tell you today that you will certainly perish, and you will not live long in the land that the Lord your God will give you, which you are crossing the Jordan to enter and inherit.
Today I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you: I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. Choose life, so that you and your descendants may live.

To love the Lord your God, to obey his voice, and to cling to him, for he is your life and the length of your days, so that you may live on the land that the Lord swore to give to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Moses finished speaking all these words to all the children of Israel.
He said to them, “I am a hundred and twenty years old today. I can no longer go in and come out. The Lord has told me, ‘You will not cross the Jordan.’”
The Lord your God is the one who goes before you. He will destroy these nations before you and let you take possession of them. Joshua is the one who goes before them, just as the Lord has said.
The Lord will do to them what he did to Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites who lived on the other side of the Jordan, and to their land, when he destroyed them.
The Lord has handed them over to you, and you are to do to them as I commanded you.

Be strong and stand firm. Do not be afraid or lose heart, and do not be alarmed before them, for the Lord your God is with you. He is the one who will go before you. He will not withdraw from you or abandon you.

And Moses called Joshua and said to him before all Israel, “Be strong and stand firm, for you are the one who will go ahead of this people into the land that the Lord swore to our ancestors to give them, and you are the one who will divide it up as an inheritance.
The Lord your God is the one who goes with you. He will not withdraw from you or abandon you. Do not be afraid or lose heart.
Moses wrote the words of this law in a book and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi who carry the ark of the Lord’s covenant, and to the elders of the children of Israel.
Moses commanded them that day, saying, “After seven years, at the appointed time in the year of release, at the Festival of Shelters,
When all Israel goes to stand before the Lord your God in the place that the Lord your God will choose, you shall read this law before all Israel, within their hearing.

when you gather the people together—the men, their wives, their children, and the foreign resident in your towns—so that they may hear and learn to fear the Lord your God and take care to carry out all the words of this law.
Their children who do not know will hear and learn to fear the Lord your God all the days that they live on the land that you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess.”

The Lord said to Moses, “Look, the days of your death are drawing near. Call Joshua, and stand together at the entrance to the tent of testimony, and I will give him his instructions.” Moses and Joshua went to the tent and stood at the entrances to the tent of testimony.
The Lord came down in a cloud and stood over the entrances to the tent of testimony.

The Lord said to Moses, “Look, you will sleep with your ancestors, and this people will rise up and prostitute themselves by following other, foreign gods of the land they are entering to possess. They will abandon me and break the covenant that I established with them.

I will turn against them in anger that day and abandon them. I will turn my face away from them, and they will be devoured. Many hardships and afflictions will overtake them. They will say that day, ‘These troubles have overtaken me because the Lord my God is not with us.’
But I will certainly turn my face away from them that day because of all the evil they have done, because they have turned to foreign gods.
Now, therefore, write down the words of this song, teach it to the children of Israel, and put it in their mouths, so that this song may be a witness for me among the children of Israel.

For I will bring them into the good land that I swore to their ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey. They will eat and be satisfied and prosper, and they will turn to foreign gods and serve them. They will provoke me and break my covenant.

This song will stand against them, testifying against them, for it will not be forgotten from the mouths of their descendants. For I know the wicked things they are doing today, before I have brought them into the good land that I swore to their ancestors.”
Moses wrote down this song that day and taught it to the children of Israel.

He commanded Joshua son of Nun, saying, “Be courageous and stand firm, for you are the one who will bring the children of Israel into the land that the Lord swore to them to give them, and he is the one who has been with you.”
When Moses had finished writing all the words of this law in a book, to the very end,
he commanded the Levites who carried the ark of the Lord’s covenant, saying,
“Take the book of this law and put it beside the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, so that it may be there as a witness against you.
For I know your stubbornness and the hardness of your neck. Even today, while I am still alive among you, you have been provoking God. How could you not provoke him again after my death?

So gather before me the leaders of your tribes, your elders, your judges, and your scribes who teach, so that I may speak all these words in their hearing and call heaven and earth to witness against them.

For I know that after my death you will act lawlessly and abandon the way that I commanded you to follow. These afflictions will overtake you in the last days, because you will do evil in the Lord’s sight, provoking him with the works of your hands.”
Moses spoke the words of this song in the hearing of the whole assembly, to its very end.
The Song. Listen, heaven, and I will speak. Let the earth listen to the words of my mouth.
Let my voice be awaited like rain, and let my words come down like dew, like water upon a plant and like snow upon grass.
For I have proclaimed the name of the Lord. Ascribe greatness to our God.
God—his works are true, and all his works are just. He is a faithful God, with no injustice in him. The Lord is righteous and holy.
We have sinned, being defiled children who are not his, a crooked and perverse generation.
Is this what you will repay the Lord? Is this the way of a foolish people without wisdom? Is he not your father, who made you his own? He made you and formed you.
Remember the days of old. Consider the years of generation after generation. Ask your father, and he will tell you. Ask your elders, and they will explain it to you.
When the Most High divided the nations, when he scattered the children of Adam, he established the boundaries of the nations according to the number of God’s angels.
The Lord’s portion was his people Jacob; Israel was his allotted inheritance.
He provided for him in the wilderness, in burning thirst. He went around with him in a waterless place and taught him. He guarded him like the pupil of an eye.
Like an eagle spreading itself over its young, he hovered over his offspring. He spread his wings, took them to himself, and lifted them onto his shoulders.
The Lord alone cared for them, and no foreign god was with them.
He brought them up onto the strength of the land and fed them with the produce of the fields. He made them eat honey from a rock and oil from a flint rock,
butter from cattle and milk from sheep, with the fat of lambs, and rams, [?] calves, and goats, and the rich kernels of wheat. He drank wine, the blood of the grape.
Jacob ate, drank, and grew fat. The beloved one kicked out; he became fat, stout, and broad. He abandoned the God who made him and turned away from God his Savior.
They provoked me with foreign gods and angered me with their abominations.
They offered sacrifices to demons, not to God—to gods they did not know, new ones that had arisen and appeared, whom their fathers did not know.
But you abandoned God, who created you, and forgot God, who sustains you.
The Lord saw this and became jealous; he became angry because of the provocation of his sons and daughters.
He said, “I will turn my face away from them and show them what will happen to them in the end, because they are a crooked generation, children who have no faithfulness in them.
They made me jealous with things that are not gods, and angered me with their idols. I too will make them jealous with what is not a nation; I will provoke them with a foolish nation.
For a fire has been kindled by my anger. It will burn down to the depths of the underworld. It will consume the earth and its produce; it will set the foundations of the mountains on fire.
I will heap disasters upon them and destroy them with my arrows.

They will waste away from hunger and become food for birds. They will be dragged backward without relief. I will send the teeth of wild beasts against them, along with the venom of creatures that crawl on the ground.
Outside, a sword will leave them childless, and terror will come from within their rooms: a young man and a virgin, a nursing child and an old man of advanced age.
I said, ‘I will scatter them and remove their memory from among humankind,’

except for the anger of their enemies, so that they would not live long, and so that their enemies would not rise against them and say, ‘Our hand is mighty, and it was not the Lord who did all these things.’
For they are a nation that has abandoned counsel, and there is no wisdom in them.
They did not reflect so as to understand these things. Let them take them to heart for the time to come.
How could one chase a thousand, or two put ten thousand to flight, unless God had given them up and the Lord had handed them over?
Their gods were not like our God, and our enemies are foolish.
For their vine comes from the vine of Sodom, and their branch comes from Gomorrah. Their grapes are grapes of gall; their cluster is bitter.
Their wine is the venom of dragons, and the poison of snakes that never subsides.
Are these things not gathered up with me and sealed in my storehouses?
And on the day of vengeance I will repay them, at the time when their feet slip. For the day of his destruction is near, and these things are ready for you.
For the Lord will judge his people, and he will be comforted concerning his servants. For he saw them falling apart, exhausted by affliction, and giving up.
The Lord said, “Where, then, are their gods, in whom they trusted?
You ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of the poured-out offering. Let them rise and help you, and become your protectors.
See, see that I am he, and there is no other god besides me. I am the one who will kill and give life. I will strike, and I will also heal, and no one can rescue anyone from my hands.
For I will raise my hand to heaven and swear by my right hand, and say, ‘I live forever.’
For I will sharpen my sword like lightning, and my hand will take hold of judgment. I will repay my enemies with judgment, and I will repay those who hate me.
I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will devour flesh—from the blood of the slain and the captives, from the heads of the enemy leaders.”

Heavens, rejoice with him, and let all the sons of God worship him. Nations, rejoice with his people, and let all the angels of God strengthen themselves in him. For the blood of his sons will be avenged, and he will repay his enemies with judgment. He will repay those who hate him and cleanse the land of his people.
Moses wrote this song on that day and taught it to the children of Israel. And Moses went in and spoke all the words of this law for the people to hear, he and Joshua son of Nun.
And when Moses had finished speaking with all Israel,
he said to them, “Take to heart all these words that I testify to you today, so that you may command your children to observe and carry out all the words of this law.
For this is not an empty word for you; it is your life. And because of this word, you will live many days in the land that you will cross the Jordan to enter and inherit.”
The Lord spoke with Moses on that day, saying,
“Go up onto Mount Abarim, that is, Mount Nebo, in the land of Moab opposite Jericho, and look at the land of Canaan, which I will give to the children of Israel to inherit.
Die on the mountain that you are going up, and be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people,
because you did not believe the word of the children of Israel at the water of dispute at Kadesh in the wilderness of Sinai, because you did not honor me as holy among the children of Israel.
You will see the land before you, but you will not enter it.”
And this is the blessing that Moses, the man of God, pronounced over the children of Israel, blessing them before he died.
He said, “The Lord came from Sinai and appeared to us from Seir. He shone forth from Mount Paran with the tens of thousands of Kadesh, with his angels beside him at his right hand.
The Lord honored his people, and all those who have been made holy are under your hands. They too are at your feet, and he received from his words
a law that Moses entrusted to us as an inheritance, together with the assemblies of Jacob.
And he will be ruler among the beloved one. The rulers of the peoples gathered with the tribes of Israel.
Let Reuben live, and do not let him die; let his numbers be great.
And as for the tribe of Judah: Lord, hear the voice of Judah and bring him to his people. Let his hands contend for him; they will plead his cause. And you will be his helper against his enemies.”
And he said to Levi, “Give Levi his signs, and his truth to the holy man whom they tested with a trial and cursed at the water of contention,
who says to his father and his mother, ‘I have not seen you.’ He did not acknowledge his brothers, and he left his own children behind, keeping your words and holding fast to your covenant.
They will proclaim your ordinances to Jacob and your law to Israel. They will offer incense in your anger at all times upon your altar.
Lord, bless his strength and accept the works of his hands. Break the hips of his enemies who have risen against him, and do not let those who hate him raise their heads.”
And he said to Benjamin, “The one beloved by the Lord will dwell securely. God will shelter him all the days, and he rested among his mountains.”
And he said to Joseph, “His land has the Lord’s blessing, from the regions of heaven and the dew, and from the abundant springs of the deep.
And its produce comes through God, from the sun’s cycles and from the completion of the months,
from the height of the mountain peaks and from the height of the everlasting hills,

and from heaven and the fullness of the earth. May the things acceptable to the one who appeared in the bush come upon Joseph’s head and upon the crown of his head, for he was honored among his brothers.

His beauty is like that of a firstborn calf, and his horns are like the horn of a wild ox. With them he will gore all the nations together, to the ends of the earth. These are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and these are the thousands of Manasseh.
And he said to Zebulun, “Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar in his dwelling places.”
They will wipe out nations, and you will call out there and offer a sacrifice of righteousness, for the wealth of the sea will nourish you, and [?] the trade of those who live on the coast.
And to Gad he said, “Blessed is Gad as he expands. He rested like a lion, having devoured an arm and rulers.”
And he saw the first portion, for the land was divided there. Rulers will gather with leaders and peoples. He carried out the Lord’s righteousness and his judgment with Israel.
And to Dan he said, “Dan is a lion’s cub; he will leap out from Bashan.”
And to Naphtali he said, “Naphtali is filled with favor, and let him be filled with blessing from the Lord. He will inherit the sea and the west.”
And to Asher he said, “Asher is blessed by his sons, and he will be blessed among his brothers. He will dip his foot in oil.”
His [?] will be iron and bronze, and your strength will be like your days.
There is no one like God, beloved one. He who rides upon heaven is your helper and the glory of the firmament.
And the shelter of God’s rule will be beneath the strength of your arm forever. He will drive out the enemy before you, saying, “You will perish.”
And Israel will live alone, secure in the land of Jacob, in a land of grain and wine, and the sky will spread rain clouds with dew for you.

Blessed are you, Israel! What other people is like you, whom the Lord saves? Your helper will fight for you, and so will the sword in which you boast. Your enemies will lie to you, and you will tread on their necks.
Moses went up onto the plains of Moab, onto Mount Nebo, onto the summit of Pisgah, opposite Jericho. And the Lord showed him all the land of Gilead, as far as Dan,
and all the land of Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah, as far as the western sea,
and the wilderness and the region around Jericho, the city of Phoenician palms, as far as Zoar.

And the Lord said to Moses, “This is the land about which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying to them, ‘I will give it to your descendants.’ I have let your eyes see it, but you will not enter it.”
And Moses, the servant of the Lord, died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the Lord.
And they buried him in Gai, near Beth-peor, and no one knows his burial place to this day.
Moses was 120 years old when he died, and his eyes had neither grown dim nor failed.
And the children of Israel mourned Moses in the plains of Moab beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho, for thirty days. When the days of mourning and weeping for Moses were completed,
Joshua son of Nun was filled with a spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hand on him. And the children of Israel obeyed him, doing as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And no other prophet arose in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face,
in all the signs and wonders that the Lord sent him to perform in the land of Egypt against Pharaoh, all his servants, and his land,
the great wonders and the mighty hand that Moses displayed before all Israel.
